I've played this for hours and can honestly say this is one of the most amazing games created in the last 40 years. It may even be better than Undertale.
Firstly, i'm going to talk about the story, and what an amazing indepth story it is. The characters are all realistic and react like anyone in the real world, the plot is developed at a thoughtful pace obviously being worked on around the clock to perfection, and the villain is just pure evil, I don't think i've wanted a villain to die more than them.
Next, the world is amazing. The detail is to the point of being too much, but that is not a bad thing by any mark ande only monsters would ignore the scenery and "play the game". On top of this the character desighns and player models (Yes you can customise you character) is more indepth and interessting than any bethesda game's design, from head to toe it is all up to you, the options are endless.
Now the only downside in this game is it's sound track, it's not good enough for a game of this level. Yes, i do know that not everyone can be Toby Fox but still, i expected more going into this work of art that what i recieved. The sound track is (at best) a 9/10.
Finally- on a more positive characteristic- the game play is fabulous, the way your character moves and attacks is the work of a god everything feels and looks natural using both controller and the mouse/keyboard set-ups. It out performs every game on the market and the fps is stable 420 to boot.
In conclusion, I would recommend this game for almost everybody i meet and 80+hours are required if you are to be my friend.

Simply amazing. I haven't had this much fun since Diablo 2. This game really scratches that itch. I was disappointed with Diablo 3 and found Torchlight 2 to be fun but too cartoonish.
I am a huge fan of Titan Quest and its amazing expansion, and you can definitely feel the influence here with the excellent skill trees and class combination system.
The loot is great and often useful, and levelling up actually feels like an event and an achievement. You have the chance to think about your character and how you want him/her to develop.
The graphics are great, nice and dark. The music is awesome and definitely fits the bill.
The levels are quite varied and there are hidden places and side quests scattered around, so exploration is rewarded. The boss monsters are original and fun to fight.
The story is not the most deep and philosophical one out there, but that's not the point of games like this. Oh, you do get to influence the development of your town based on choices made during certain encounters.
The crafting system is complex and rich with possibilities of creating useful gear.
This is an early access game, although it feels pretty solid already: there is lots of content already out and more is on the way. It most certainly is worth the asking price. In my opinion these guys deserve it for delivering a great action RPG experience!
This game is for you if you like:
-Titan Quest.
-Useful loot without endless grinding.
-A genuinely dark atmosphere (à la Diablo).
-An ARPG that isn't too dumbed down.
-Proper character classes/skill trees.

Having been playing the game co-op almost the entire time I've been playing the game, I have to say it's best as a 2-player game. We've been controlling 2 characters each(you start with 2 custom ones, and you can get 2 in town), and that helps managing equipment(I handle crafting, friend handles identifying) and buying/selling(only one player needs any bartering skill for instance). The dialoge in the game, while almost all text, is well written, charming, and often funny. The interactions between party members, particularly the two leaders is a really nice quirk that can both alter stats and cause unexpected comedy between the players as they argue with eachother.
The game has a somewhat-harsh Dragon Quest syndrome at the outset, having several areas accessable early on with enemies that are too strong for your party, but there is a lot of quests and shenanigans in the first town that can get you up to around level 3 or 4, which lets you head out of town with your heads held a little higher. Crafting and Blacksmithing are rather worthwhile, the first letting you create a lot of different gear, and the latter letting you -improve- gear. Blacksmithing's particularly notable for letting you sharpen(strengthen) bladed weapons, and decrease movement penalties on heavy armor(and in fact give movement bonuses if you're particularly skilled!). Crafting helps fill out exotic equipment slots like rings and amulets easier.
It's worth noting that you can use quicksaves and quickloads (F5 and F8) to reroll loot in chests, so keep that in mind when you find a chest after a hard boss or something.
Again, the game really is best co-op, unless you really love managing 4 characters alone with minute details and inventory management. It really encourages teamwork, planning, and coordination. Do try not to set your teammates on fire, or poison them, or blow them up, or telekinetically drop enemies on them, or blow up traps on them, or electrocute them in water, or anything like that if you would. Your friend doesn't deserve that... do they?
At time of writing I've played this for 3.3 hours. So I guess Half life 3 confirmed?

Divinity: Original Sin does something impressive here--it takes "old school" RPGs in to the modern age, and it does it quite impressively.
I'm not going to fool around here, I LOVE this game. It completely embraces the concept that not everyone can be good at everything, and that sometimes a game isn't your cup of tea. I adore the idea that the folks at Larian took the time to craft a masterpiece for the halls of RPG history. Incorportating vast maps, myriads of quests, brilliant tactical combat, and content out the wazoo, D:OS is nothing but a gamer's delight.
Be warned, this isn't a casual game! Combat is challenging and requires thought. You will die, but thankfully, Larian lets you save at will, including during combat, so if you make a bad choice, just go back and keep trying.
I cannot recommend this game enough, and it is my sincere hope that the success of Divinity: Original Sin will spawn many more games like it.

Honestly - great game overall.
TL:DR - Story is a bit "meh" (disclaimer: not 100% finished yet), parkour is pretty smooth and solid (8.5/10), the melee weapons are phenomenal, the shooting is decent (7/10), zombie types are varied enough, and the gameplay is solid (9/10).
Pros
- Melee weapons are incredibly fun.
- Enough varation of zombie types.
- Parkour system is fairly smooth
- Skill trees make sense and you skill up by using the skill (parkour increases agility, killing increases power, interacting with world increases survivor).
- Devs seem genuinely decent and also have a good amount of humor. Interesting easter eggs and references throughout the world.
Neutral
- Looting. Even on hard it feels like there is too much loot but it kind of fits the games narrative if you intend to role play. The main story happens fairly quickly and is very time-sensitive but the game doesn't force a match between the day/night cycle and the story.
- Not much variety among guns and no scaling. I get that the point of the game is to go melee badass on zombies and also focus on stealth but the guns should at least scale a bit or have a way to upgrade. Basically the only time to use guns in this game is against the human factions/characters or mowing down weaker zombie types.
Cons
- Inventory. You get a globally accessible player stash but it has no panels to filter your items - it's just all one big list. It can get tiresome.
- No food/water gauge. I would love to see this implemented (even if only on hard mode or as an optional addon).

Finally a great successor to Neverwinter Nights, albiet with turn based combat. This makes an amazing RPG with that great writing and attention to detail that I expect from Larian Studios. With a enjoyable coop mode to boot, why don't you already own this?

Well folks! It's Dying Light! An extremely hyped game that people had high hopes for! And for the most part, it succeeds. First, this may be a personal opinion, but the voice acting in this game seems to be iffy on certain characters, it's just a pet peev but still for a triple A game, you need to fix your voice actors microphones, that or make them put some emotion into their voice after hearing their hubby died, mmkay? But let's get down to brass tacks shall we?
(WARNING: This will be a LONG review, with as much information as I can muster into it, so if you're looking for the essentials, you may need to find another reviewer, or maybe I'll remember to get the big things down at the bottom.)
The Cons:
1) The Parkour system could use some work, there are certain situations that a nerdy kid who hasn't been outside in a week could climb, and your guy is just like "OH Iz D@t hou we Perker!? OopSIe!" But seriously, this dude is bi-polar about his effectiveness in this parkour system that is otherwise perfectly fine.
2) HUMAN ENEMIES! If you ever wanted enemies to hate, make it these guys, for some reason these people can hit a throwing knife outta the air because they are obviously Ninjas! Oh and whenever you swing they will block it, and there is no block for their attacks and the only way to really avoid them is to use their dodge system (We will get to THAT momentarily) or the grapple, which sometimes decides not to work, and I've tested it, I'm not just some scrub-lord! There are moments where your character refuses to throw this guy with a machete off the roof.
3) The Dodge mechanic, for whatever reason, this is honestly the most useless kind of dodge system ever, there are really only two situations you'll ever need it, and in both you'll be filled with dissapointment 65% of the time. So you can move back, left, and right, pretty simple, right? Well yeah it is, but the thing is if you base certain enemies on a dodge mechanic that doesn't work properly, then you'll just be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off your consumers. One of the most annoying things in this game is when you try to dodge to the side to avoid that guy slashing at you, only to find that apparently he has the arc of a Warhammer, when he's using a Chef's knife, thus rendering only going back to effectively avoid the enemies and that gets boring and still at times, does not work.
4) The ending of the game, I'm not gonna give spoilers...But do you remember Button-mashing sequences? Yeah, I wasn't a fan of them either.
5) The story, to be fair, it's a zombie game so if you bought it for a story then you're already doing it wrong but seriously I guessed the entire plot as soon as I met the antagonist, but then again, my hindsight might just be a hinderence here. :P
Finally after sifting thru the bad, and occasionally the ugly! Let's move onto the good!
The Pros:
1) You can feel like the Ultimate zombie killing machine seriously, sometimes you just get these moments where you can jump down from a roof, stab that dude, throw a knife (granted if he didn't block it -_-) to stun that guy, slash his buddy and finish off the guy you threw a knife into. Seriously, there will be moments where you feel like you own the world and I like that, so hats off to ya ladies & gents!
2) The Parkour is pretty free-flowing, aside from the few situations as I said above, you can pretty much run, jump, and slide everywhere and it helps you move around the map FAR quicker than if you had to take all the backroads and dig a hole to China to get to objective A only to go to checkpoint B with even more frustration.
3) Guns, yes, yes, guns, I know there's a huge debacle wether or not a zombie game should be reliant on guns, but I feel this game has done a pretty swell job of getting it right. They don't give you super over-powered guns, nor do they give you much ammo, thus making the player conserve ammunition, and keep to your Melee weapon as your main source of damage until you REALLY need those bullets.
4) The side quests, these things actually give you some really cool stuff! Seriously, there's one in perticular that I did and I'm still using the tools the quest provided me with, just because it was an actually effective weapon that can last me quite a while.
5) The amount of weapons, seems to be pretty expansive, there's one-handed, and two-handed weapons that both obtain different points for as you level up, which yes there is a leveling up system, which will be addressed shortly. I can honestly say that I've only had to use the same looking weapon about twice, the rest of the time it seemed to have unique features that others did not, not to mention some of these weapons look awesome! And you'll feel awesome afer you slab a battery on it, and shock that zombies face off!
6) Multi-player, as always, butchering zombies with your friends is a blast, and you'll have funny stories reffering to "Your hammer, goes in, but doesn't always come out" plus, maybe you could work in a little imagination and make a role-playing thing out of it! I dunno, I'm just spitballing here.
7) The game at night, seriously, when you're wandering around this game at night you'll feel like there is something behind you, a LOT probably because there are several things behind you, two of which are seven feet tall and have an exceptional hankering for human flesh, although after a while it won't be as bad, you'll still have your fair share of jump-scares and creepy moments (Side note! There is one quest in particular that did it really well! I loved the sequence and I think that they should try doing it more in later games.)
To wrap this up we're gonna go over the Largest points of the game starting with the bad
Cons:
-Your character randomly forgetting how to climb that fence right there that you can most definetly climb.
-Human enemies are annoying and you will want to find and kill their families (if they're still alive.)
-Dodging feels really stupid and is very rarely actually useful.
-The end of the game, seriously you guys, if you are a true gamer you'll understand the sin committed here.
-The story, although this is relatively little because it's a zombie game, this one felt really cliche.
Pros:
-This game effectively makes you feel like you are indeed the Terminator himself
-Parkour is rather free-flowing and effective at getting around the maps.
-Guns aren't OP and they don't give you enough ammo to take over Africa single-handedly.
-Side quests are actually rewarding and can give you some pretty nifty equipment, especially later on in the game.
-The Sheer amount of melee weapons, gives you a big sense of "Oooh! Which one to pick! Decisions, decisions."
-Multi-player is fun, running around a map full of zombies is fun, although the PvP mode is a little iffy at first, with a little practice and patience, it can be extremely fun and heart-pounding
-This game has an amazing ability to become a horror game withing seconds, (specifically referring to night-time) and honestly, I like that a lot because it keeps the player on edge, and makes sure you don't run around like a dingus all the time.

Tried this for 30 minutes in PUBG (game is still having performance issues due to it being a early access game).
Now before i go any further, yes, i do qualify as a low-end user, and run a laptop with the following specifications:
I5-6200u @ 2.40Ghz
Intel Graphics 520 and Nvidia Geforce 920MX (Nvidia one is used by default in games)
12GB DDR4 memory
Now, i don't need alot of time to know and see if this does work or not, was skeptical and did want to see if it did make any difference, the answer to this is simple: It does nothing different then what Razer Cortex (freeware), Advanced Systemcare (has a build in Turbo Mode), Wise Game Booster, or any other free game booster can do.
Ran PUBG with this on for 30 minutes, and can say that those are the only 2 things i noticed, 1 Very small change that it didn't matter, and 1 negative one.
First, Can this increase FPS or make you run things on higher settings then you normally would? no, it cannot.
All this does it stopping processes, and this 'constraining' your OS from the game, is just a hoax.
The only little thing i have noticed: the Loading into the game went a little faster, and the textures loaded in a little faster aswell, but that was it, no FPS difference at all or any other improvement.
The second thing, which is negative: I noticed with CPUCores running, it gave me some Stuttering again, and a almost freeze in-game.
Short but Straight to the point: Avoid buying this, no matter what, this program is not capable of anything more then any of the free game boosters out there, and even those do little to nothing.
Hope you all keep your money for games instead, as for me, a refund request is handed in after those 30 minutes.

This game is by far one of the biggest mind♥♥♥♥s I've had in video games (I've yet to experience LSD: dream simulator) and quite an interesting journey, and also one that has a good amount of life lessons.
Gameplay
Unlike the design of the levels and how most of them don't seemt to lead to somewhere the game itself is very simple to understand. You are tasked to perform some actions either using platforming skills or with your gun that you'll get later in the game.
As for the design of the levels is one of the most confusing ones I've experienced in my life, but not necesary a bad one since they're kinda easy to follow, they're well designed and not frustrating (but the frustration comes to your skills) and besides you have a map to help you go though places you've visited before. But good luck with your sense of direction since you'll probably be lost.
The puzzles are very creative and one of the strongest points of the game, I like them a lot and I'll probably replay the game after I tackle some of the other games I have on hold.
Controls
Very tight and responisve. I haven't experienced delays nor have I have trouble with controling the protagonist nor the gun.
Story
It's a simple story, go through the maze, escape the maze
so it's as simple as it gets and even if I put the ending as a spoiler you're not playing the game for the story.
Graphics
Gorgeous and simple. While by today's standards they're okay and look nice, they look pretty and it seems that they showed care towards making the assets. And yet this simplistic design is capable or rendering some interesting levels and mind♥♥♥♥ing moments.
Sountrack
The songs are relaxing and a good method to calm you in order to progress to the game (since it takes a lot of patience). Personally they're not something that I'll look forward to listening. But check them out if you end up liking them.
Overrall
Fantastic game to get if you're a fan of puzzle games, and if you want a journey of constant mind♥♥♥♥s and a weird maze then you'll like what this game has to offer. With solid controls, good gameplay and good sountrack you'll have a good treat. Just make sure that you'll have time to play this since it does require a lot of time to finish it

If you don't want to read all of this here's the short of it: I love this game. Plain and simple. It's stunningly gorgeous, extremely well animated, and the story is very compelling and moving. It has it's flaws, but I don't find these flaws severe enough to keep myself or anyone from playing this game. It's basically Fire Emblem crossed with Oregon Trail. If that
sounds good to you then, by all means, buy this game. You'll have a blast.
Now that that's out of the way, let me explain the shortcomings of this game that I've experienced. There are, by my reckoning, two major problems. One is the options menu. The other appears to be a mild stability issue which may or may not affect you.  In the course of my sessions I've found that during extended periods of gameplay it tends to suddenly go into a window and become unresponsive. Effectively leaving me no choice but to force quit via the task manager. Otherwise it runs very smoothly with no drops in frame-rate.
Secondly, the options menu is practically non-existent. You can, somewhat, adjust sound by clicking on some icons that don't  really explain themselves very well or switch from full-screen to windowed--and that's about it. Granted, the game was set up so well that I didn't feel like I needed to change anything in the options menu. But still, it's nice to have a wide array of options.
Aside from the options menu and the fact that it seems to crash from being played for too long--it's a fantastic game!
I have thoroughly enjoyed my time with the Banner Saga. The only thing that I think could make it better, aside from fixing the flaws mentioned above, would be to add more content--new character classes, more story/quests etc. I especially wish that all the cutscenes could have been animated like the opening one. But it's understandable that they could not maintain that throughout. I have some minor issues with how the story ended. It seems like they may be trying for a sequel at some point since a lot of questions were left unanswered. Hopefully Stoic was successful enough with this that they can expand upon the story and world with future releases.
All in all, I had a lot of fun with it. If you love strategy games then you'll love this.

So I'm not going to give it a thumbs down, but I will say that despite how much I wanted to enjoy this game, it just wasn't for me.
First off, yes, I have less than an hour of gameplay, not nearly enough time put in to give any sort of review. So I will say that I would still recommend this game, as I do like the concept, but I just felt that me personally wouldn't be putting much time into it.
So for the Pros;
~   Beautiful scenery and well optimized. Very rarely would I have any kind of fps drop.
~   As a long time snowboarding fan, I like how it feels like, well, snowboarding. It has a slight arcade feeling, but for the most part it doesn't feel over the top.
~   Squirrel suit is pretty fun. Fast and can be a bit tricky, but still fun.
~   I like the idea of an open world, desipte me not putting the time in to actually explore, the freedom of being able to  choose where you want to go, or start is pretty cool.
Cons; (Just me personally)
~   I didn't really care for the controls too much, and yes, I was using and xbox one controller. It just feels a bit odd and clunky.
~   Over saturation of tutorials. I am the kind of person, whether it be a movie or a game, if I'm not sucked in pretty quick I'll lose interest. So spending the first 20 or so minutes of the game going through the motions of the different sports, locations, line challenges, etc... was a bit of a turn off. I like to be placed in a world and have to just figure the game out. Much like Dark Souls I guess you could say.
~   Always online: While this isn't a huge problem for me personally I could see how it could be for others. I spend a lot of time away from home in hotels, so trying to do any online gaming on unstable hotel wifi isn't the most fun thing in the world.
So overall I would give it a 5/10. Which is a shame because I really wanted to love this game. While the lack of arcade is what was appealing to me, maybe that's what this game needs more of. So if you're a wintersports fan, I still recommend this game. But if you're anything like me, and some of these cons outweighted the pros, then I would suggest holding off until a price drop, or maybe some tweaks and/or content patches.

Also, the AI is very incompetent. They often fail to attack with ranged units properly, and frequently move their units back and forth WITHIN RANGE OF YOUR UNITS/CITIES for seemingly no reason.

Still, all in all the game is very good. The AI is just plain bad though.

Although I have not played the game for too long, I believe I have played it enough to write a review about it. So for all of you that are a little bit pushed away by the game's "steep" price, this might help you out a little bit.
The game is a sports game that is based around skiing, snowboarding, paragliding, and flying in a wingsuit around some big mountains (just in case you haven't figured that out yet). It is made by Ubisoft which is somewhat unfortunate due to the fact that you have to have a UPlay account for the game and Ubisoft is known for its incompetence. Despite that information it is a really solid and fun game. The controls are user-friendly which enhances the experience of dashing down a snow-covered mountain at maximum velocity. For those who have an amazing computer, you will likely find that the graphics are amazing and for those with a relatively bad computer, you will find slightly less amazing graphics, but stil amazing! Basically, the graphics are pretty sick. The gameplay is extremely awesome too (for the most part). Snowboarding and skiing are both the biggest highlights of this game compared to the other two sports to choose from. I guess the wingsuits are okay, but honestly, the paragliding is pretty boring. Despite that, the gameplay is pretty sick and definitely makes you feel like you are actually skiing or snowboarding.
This game is great for both sportspeople and gamers a like, which is helpful because it allows for more players and a large variety of players. Although I haven't really done much with the social aspect of the game because none of my friends own this game, the little I have seen of it seems to be pretty solid. One thing that is really cool about the game is that it is an open world game so it feels like you have more freedom to just do what you want. You can either do the challenges or you can just mess around by snowboarding down giant hills or maybe faceplanting into a giant boulder in a wingsuit. The possibilities are almost endless.
There really is not a lot to say negatively about this game. The main things that are negative about the game are the paragliding, Ubisoft, and not a lot of stat progression (which really is not a problem for me but it could be for most people). This game also has couple of bugs every now and then which comes with Ubisoft, but those could possibly be worse due to the fact that my computer is not that great.
Although the game is some what pricey, it is most definitely worth it on a sale and still worth it even when it is not on a sale assuming you aren't breaking the bank by buying this game.

(Which I realize is a lot to ask, unfair, self-contradictory...)
Anyway, I absolutely love the art (I always keep on going on about how it's the art direction, not the poly count that really make the difference, and it's nice to be proven right once in a while) and enjoy the combat and the story, but can't help but wish there was more of an RPG there - as it is, it's more like an extremely beautiful "choose your own adventure" book with fun turn based combat interludes. I would absolutely recommend it, but some aspects of it leave me hugely frustrated.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is incredibly fun. I love turn based games and this takes strategy to the fullest. In this game it is man vs. alien and we are fighting back to remove the aliens. You control a squad of soldiers that you move and tell them who to attack, defend, or to do overwatch to attack moving enemies. There are four types of soldiers you can get randomly when they level up and each will gain rank and you choose from 1 or 2 abilities when they do. If your soldiers die you have a chance to save them by healing them before they die but if they die they are gone forever. You also have the build up your forces by researching technology and spending resources to buy new technologies, weapons, and buildings.
This is a highly addictive game which can be pretty difficult if you don't cheat (save often and reload over and over again to get the best results). An interesting thing about XCom is it saves its random number generator so that means if you load a game and do the same actions over again you will get the same results but if you do things in a different order you can get different results (the chances to hit will be the same but if one soldier is more likely to hit, he might hit an enemy when another would miss).
The only thing I didn't like about this game is it seems to be very short to finish one playthrough but you could always play again with a higher difficulty or it also comes with Second Wave which lets you chance certain settings in the game. I would highly recommend if you like turn based strategy games.

Well folks! It's Dying Light! An extremely hyped game that people had high hopes for! And for the most part, it succeeds. First, this may be a personal opinion, but the voice acting in this game seems to be iffy on certain characters, it's just a pet peev but still for a triple A game, you need to fix your voice actors microphones, that or make them put some emotion into their voice after hearing their hubby died, mmkay? But let's get down to brass tacks shall we?
(WARNING: This will be a LONG review, with as much information as I can muster into it, so if you're looking for the essentials, you may need to find another reviewer, or maybe I'll remember to get the big things down at the bottom.)
The Cons:
1) The Parkour system could use some work, there are certain situations that a nerdy kid who hasn't been outside in a week could climb, and your guy is just like "OH Iz D@t hou we Perker!? OopSIe!" But seriously, this dude is bi-polar about his effectiveness in this parkour system that is otherwise perfectly fine.
2) HUMAN ENEMIES! If you ever wanted enemies to hate, make it these guys, for some reason these people can hit a throwing knife outta the air because they are obviously Ninjas! Oh and whenever you swing they will block it, and there is no block for their attacks and the only way to really avoid them is to use their dodge system (We will get to THAT momentarily) or the grapple, which sometimes decides not to work, and I've tested it, I'm not just some scrub-lord! There are moments where your character refuses to throw this guy with a machete off the roof.
3) The Dodge mechanic, for whatever reason, this is honestly the most useless kind of dodge system ever, there are really only two situations you'll ever need it, and in both you'll be filled with dissapointment 65% of the time. So you can move back, left, and right, pretty simple, right? Well yeah it is, but the thing is if you base certain enemies on a dodge mechanic that doesn't work properly, then you'll just be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off your consumers. One of the most annoying things in this game is when you try to dodge to the side to avoid that guy slashing at you, only to find that apparently he has the arc of a Warhammer, when he's using a Chef's knife, thus rendering only going back to effectively avoid the enemies and that gets boring and still at times, does not work.
4) The ending of the game, I'm not gonna give spoilers...But do you remember Button-mashing sequences? Yeah, I wasn't a fan of them either.
5) The story, to be fair, it's a zombie game so if you bought it for a story then you're already doing it wrong but seriously I guessed the entire plot as soon as I met the antagonist, but then again, my hindsight might just be a hinderence here. :P
Finally after sifting thru the bad, and occasionally the ugly! Let's move onto the good!
The Pros:
1) You can feel like the Ultimate zombie killing machine seriously, sometimes you just get these moments where you can jump down from a roof, stab that dude, throw a knife (granted if he didn't block it -_-) to stun that guy, slash his buddy and finish off the guy you threw a knife into. Seriously, there will be moments where you feel like you own the world and I like that, so hats off to ya ladies & gents!
2) The Parkour is pretty free-flowing, aside from the few situations as I said above, you can pretty much run, jump, and slide everywhere and it helps you move around the map FAR quicker than if you had to take all the backroads and dig a hole to China to get to objective A only to go to checkpoint B with even more frustration.
3) Guns, yes, yes, guns, I know there's a huge debacle wether or not a zombie game should be reliant on guns, but I feel this game has done a pretty swell job of getting it right. They don't give you super over-powered guns, nor do they give you much ammo, thus making the player conserve ammunition, and keep to your Melee weapon as your main source of damage until you REALLY need those bullets.
4) The side quests, these things actually give you some really cool stuff! Seriously, there's one in perticular that I did and I'm still using the tools the quest provided me with, just because it was an actually effective weapon that can last me quite a while.
5) The amount of weapons, seems to be pretty expansive, there's one-handed, and two-handed weapons that both obtain different points for as you level up, which yes there is a leveling up system, which will be addressed shortly. I can honestly say that I've only had to use the same looking weapon about twice, the rest of the time it seemed to have unique features that others did not, not to mention some of these weapons look awesome! And you'll feel awesome afer you slab a battery on it, and shock that zombies face off!
6) Multi-player, as always, butchering zombies with your friends is a blast, and you'll have funny stories reffering to "Your hammer, goes in, but doesn't always come out" plus, maybe you could work in a little imagination and make a role-playing thing out of it! I dunno, I'm just spitballing here.
7) The game at night, seriously, when you're wandering around this game at night you'll feel like there is something behind you, a LOT probably because there are several things behind you, two of which are seven feet tall and have an exceptional hankering for human flesh, although after a while it won't be as bad, you'll still have your fair share of jump-scares and creepy moments (Side note! There is one quest in particular that did it really well! I loved the sequence and I think that they should try doing it more in later games.)
To wrap this up we're gonna go over the Largest points of the game starting with the bad
Cons:
-Your character randomly forgetting how to climb that fence right there that you can most definetly climb.
-Human enemies are annoying and you will want to find and kill their families (if they're still alive.)
-Dodging feels really stupid and is very rarely actually useful.
-The end of the game, seriously you guys, if you are a true gamer you'll understand the sin committed here.
-The story, although this is relatively little because it's a zombie game, this one felt really cliche.
Pros:
-This game effectively makes you feel like you are indeed the Terminator himself
-Parkour is rather free-flowing and effective at getting around the maps.
-Guns aren't OP and they don't give you enough ammo to take over Africa single-handedly.
-Side quests are actually rewarding and can give you some pretty nifty equipment, especially later on in the game.
-The Sheer amount of melee weapons, gives you a big sense of "Oooh! Which one to pick! Decisions, decisions."
-Multi-player is fun, running around a map full of zombies is fun, although the PvP mode is a little iffy at first, with a little practice and patience, it can be extremely fun and heart-pounding
-This game has an amazing ability to become a horror game withing seconds, (specifically referring to night-time) and honestly, I like that a lot because it keeps the player on edge, and makes sure you don't run around like a dingus all the time.

The game revolvers around you as the unnamed commander of the XCOM project which is humanities first and last line of defense from the alien menace. Now one criticism turn based strategy like civilization 5 is that it takes for ever for anything to happen, now this is in place for a good reason after all any chess game where you can get checkmate in just one move would be boring. While the is in slow pace in base management in combat everything happens instantly, in just one move you solider could get a critical hit by an alien or the other way around creating a feeling on being on a knife's edge especially the higher the difficulty. There are some flaws; the interception is tacked on, the thin men are a bit too much of a difficulty spike when introduced and the random generation on the steam caves means just a reason to start a new campaign as soon as you started. These however are all minor flaws a perfect game the simplicity and fragility makes the tactics rewarding and since each play through is different with varying difficult levels to choose from makes this game a must buy.

the ugly:
- buggy and unpolished in many ways... Some times you get kicked out from the match. Guns become invinsible. You shot the person but did no dmg. Price of the items of the store does not appear correctly and this has not been fixed for a long time. and so on.
- spawn killing is common and they don't have a good solution for it. They added a system where you become invulnerable briefly after you spawn but simultaneously you cant deal dmg so nothing really changes. You just get to get out from your spawn a little further.
- stupid "stacking" in match making. Ideally, you wud want players to join team 1 and team 2 in an alternating order so that the number of players in both teams are close to equal. Whats happening instead is that players can choose to join one team while there are barely any players in the other team, so whats left out is a 3 v 9 match... Very fair.
- Once you reach lvl 20, you are matched against players that are lvl 20 to 35. The max tier for armors and dmg can be reached at lvl 28, which means until lvl 28 from lvl 20, you are constantly beaten up by players with higher tier gears. You also level up very slowely during this time period so you really have to grind it through until lvl 28. Btw, until lvl 20, the game is less competitive and there are far less players with premium weapons, so the game is less stressful until then.
- Pricing is ridiculous for premium weapons. A typical price for a premium weapon is 15 dollars (and pretty much you have to pay real money if you want to buy one of them, even though theoretically you can buy them without real money)
- Premium weapons and vehicles can be over powered, especially vehicles. A good examples is how this premium attack heli called KA52 Alligator can easily wipe out bronze, ground vehicles and currently there are no effective way to counter it except for using a KA52 Alligator. So if your team doesnt have the heli, your team is basically ♥♥♥♥ed up.
- there are no scores that counts assists so its either you kill or not. Pretty damn annoying time to time.
The good:
- you can run this game on a potato
- the soldiers make a silly voice when they die
- you can still enjoy the game with bronze, unlockable weapons.
- 7 maps where 3 of them are big, vehicle maps
- although it will be difficult to purchase what you want due to the pricing, you can still buy clothes and stuff like that in the store to customize your character
- you can leave the match anytime you want
- you can switch between 1st POV and 3rd POV mode so you can intentionally use 3rd POV to scout enemies and do surprise mother ♥♥♥♥er!! when they come close to you.
- variety of game modes so its hard to get bored
Overall:
Cashgrab P2W FPS with variety of game modes, guns, vehicles and gears. And dont forget that org asm voice the soldiers make when they die.

If your looking for a polished version of the original game this isn't it. This game is fun in its own right though.
Pro's- fun tactical play, good graphics, decent interface.
Cons- Dumbed down from the original game, 2/3 lose of faction even if you win. Resources are low making it difficult to manage anything, here you are a world funded organization and you can only afford to make a few guns a month with a meger squad of soldiers to defend the world. Tactical map is dumbed down too all the great things about the original tactical map are gone and control is limited.
My opinion of the game is a bit bias as a long time xcom supporter, this game is a 7-8/10 for todays game genre, to an xcom fan it would probably be rated 3-4/10 (sadly). Here is why-
Things the game needs-
-Multiple bases
-Multiple ships with multiple squads
-A way to not lose 2/3 world faction every battle (there might be a loophole but I havent found it)
-Allow patrols (anywhere I choose)
-seperate sqauds
-None dumbed down character progression (why does the world find WoW so interesting, is everyone incapable of thinking for themself.)
- Non linear gameplay
-actual radar (not this satalite bs an alien would just shoot it down we have no defenses up there)
-Its just so off base from the original its an entirely diffrent game and the name should be changed to alien invasion a losing battle or somthing.
-You will find hundreds of posts by fans complaining about this title simply because they slapped a xcom tag on it, it is not xcom: ufo defense. Infact its so dumbed down its and insult to to the original ufo defense game. They used 9+gb of disk space on this game and only achieved 3/10 of the play value the original 4-6mb (I don't even think it was that big) game offers.
Thats mainly the problem with game development these days- Games are developed for graphics and mindless gameplay. When graphics were terrible the game had to have depth and content to be apealing, then the WoW generation was born. Automated stat asignment  with less control, less customization, less options- install, play and don't think. Now this is a tactical game but leveling your squad is limited and dumbed down. Choices really don't matter. The original didn't really have any choices but the leveling system was better, more missions more kills = more rank better stats and carring heavier weapons. Gameplay had an echo affect. This game is way to linear to have any echo.
I will reccomend the game to anyone that hasn't played the original, anyone that has played the original I will not because the depression caused by your purchase could very well burry you its really that sad in comparison.

I bought Grim Dawn after watching a Twitch stream. Having not heard of this game before I spent some time researching as I have been burned by early access games before. After reading and watching and rinsing and repeating I finally broke down and bought Grim Dawn. I have not been disappointed so far. The game is visually stunning and controls very well. It does not hold your hand and requires exploration and actual reading of the quests. The world is also an open one with load screens only when entering caves or dungeons. Transportation is alieviated by a nice portal system though, which makes getting around to those areas already discovered a breeze. The skill system seems very robust allowing for a mashup of two specs (unlocked at level 10) and making or breaking your build interesting and rewarding. It seems like the developers are quite active in rolling out updates. Like any early access game though, I am sure there are problems which I havn't encountered or noticed yet. So as I do recommend this game, remember do your own homework. Grim Dawn is a nice breath of fresh air in the stale ARPG realm. 3.8/5 Bitz

I really like this game, if you were unfortunate enough to get this when it first came out and you had a nvidia GPU you most likely would not agree with me due to all the permonace issues and game crashes etc etc. but thanks to the latest patches this game now plays flawlessly.
The graphics on this game are awesome providing that your GPU can handle it but one tip i found was to set your view distance to minimum as it does not make much of a difference and you can push around another 10FPS out the game, also motion blur and film grain effect give you a few more frames if disabled.
The gameplay is great; free-running whilst smashing zombies up, what not to like? A wide range of activities, chalenges, side quests, colectables and decent leveling system will keep you busy for hours. I got over 50 hours out of it but at least 10 of these hours were played after i had got everything in game. Online is rather active and you shouldnt have any issues finding groups.
I definately recomend this game but make sure that your system meets the minimum requirements as quite a few people have thought that their system could run it only to be dissapointed or end up playing on much lower graphics settings.
If you like Dead Island, you will like this. Think of Dead Island crossed with Mirrors edge and it should give a pretty good idea of what to expect.

I've been playing survival horror since before Resident Evil and have played everything from that to Killing Floor, to Left 4 Dead, to Outlast, and more.  That said, there's rarely a game that is unique and fresh enough to really catch my interest for more than a few hours at a time.  This game fortunately is one of them!
I am about 78% through my first play through and this game is amazing.  It comes as no surprise that there's some heavy Dead Island influence here which is easily explained away by reading that some of the devs from it helped produce this title.  In a nutshell it's Dead Island mixed with Mirror's Edge.  Parkour fighting in a fairly large open world.  I say that because it's not extensive like games like Stalker or other free roaming games, but the indivudual worlds and sub maps inside the city of Harran are big enough that the game doesn't get stale.  And yet the map is small enough that treking through it isn't tedious without some sort of fast travel system (which is not present in this game).  Edit there is one fast travel station but it only takes you back and forth from the first main map to the second.  You basically progress through the missions and side missions which are tied to an excellent story and decent character acting.
As you go along the way you can find or buy weapons which have a limited life but can be repaired a few times.  You can craft new weapons and upgrade existing weapons making them stronger, more durable, and easier to handle/swing as well as applying elemental effects that do even more bonus damage.  The weapon upgrade system seems like it progresses in good timing with the story as your progress.  You also gain the ability to use the items you find and upgrade and craft even newer more powerful and useful items.  This game relies heavily on scavenging as building upgrades for your weapons as well as crafting items are needed to perform the said crafting.   You use "survivor sense" to detect when you're near items you can acquire.  And the sense is color coded to the items as well.  So it's important especially in the beginning to search everything your survivor sense finds.  Oh and just like in Borderlands weapons are also color coded by damage/level and once again, Gold seems to be the top level weapon with White/Gray at the bottom with Green, Blue, and Violet levels in ascending order.  Naturally as you progress you'll find weapons in a higher color class do less damage so those of you who enjoyed the 2K weapon system in Borderlands will feel right at home.
You have 3 main skill trees each with their own experience points which is a nice change from one XP tree.  These will be your tools for survival and make you better at staying alive and more effective at killing zombies.
SURVIVOR - A skill tree that you use to unlock abilities to craft new items, get an edge on traders for better deals, improve your abilities of searching and detecting items, as well as tricks for staying alive like camouflaging in zombie guts to avoid detection.  The final ability in the tree allows you to use all you've learner more effectively at level 25.
AGILITY - A skill tree based on speed and well... agility.  Unlocking items in this skill tree will give you new abilities and techniques to run, jump, scale building, and improve your hand to hand fighting technique against zombies, as well as give you escape tactics when cornered.  This is all the Parkour aspect of the game where you basically learn to leap and bound from building to building effortlessly stepping on the heads of zombies, and grappling them and throwing them aside.  The final ability in the tree for level 24 is that you won't get tired from running or jumping.
POWER - This is the tree I focused on first.  while still gaining points on the other skill trees.  Unlocking items in this skill tree gives you the ability to kill more effectively and efficiently by giving you stronger attacks and unlocking new attack and kill methods.  One of the most critical skills here is the ability to kill a zombie when it's down.  In the beginning this was a life saver so I didn't ruin all my weapons.  After a while though you do get strong enough that you'll be able to take down clusters of zombies with a strong weapon.  The final ability in the power tree gives you the ability to swing your weapon and fight without getting tired.  This was the biggest deal for me so I can swing my weapon over and over when surrounded.
I've put almost 60 hours into this game and it's a tremendously good amount of fun.  And even moreso if you do a couple missions or play the whole game in Co-Op mode with 2-3 freinds.  If the game seems a bit easy once you get leveled up there's a hard mode.  The DLC challenges are fun for a pass or two but not necessary to enjoy the game.  I loved the go anywhere and climb anything aspect of the game but have to say although the power challenges weren't too bad, I didn't enjoy the Parkour challenges as much as I do love freerunning in other games (because in real life I would just end up hurting myself LOL).
I believe this game is one of those titles that earns the full pricetag, but if you can get a deal all the more reason to pick it up and enjoy!

Divinity: Original Sin returns to the old turn-based RPG gametypes, honouring old favourites like Baldur's Gate with the familiar fantasy RPG setting.
A group of adventurers, titled 'Source Hunters', do exactly what their their titles indicate; a special type of magic known as 'source' has a particularly bad habit of corrupting those who use it ('Sourcerers', HAH), and often these Source-users end up going crazy or mad with power, and becoming more trouble than the locals can handle. That's when these guys step in and relieve the world of this blight. On your band's first assignment, a seemingly routine case of 'hordes-of-undead-threatening-to-take-over-town', they get pulled into circumstances far greater and more disasterous than they could have imagined. With the very fate of Cyseal depending on their ability to find out what's going on they need to stop it from taking over everything...
The most notable part of this game for me is the customization. Not only do you have 11 preset classes to play, ranging from Warrior to Wizard, from Ranger to Rogue and everything inbetween you could expect in a fantasy RPG, but you can tweak each class right down to its core starting skills, spells,  abilities and traits to suit your preferred playstyle before embarking. The character creation is a little bit lacking in one or two areas; you have a choice of three voices for each gender, all six of which are clearly caucasian, and all sound like the same person pitching their accents and tones to sound either more intellectual, rugged or righteous, depensing on which one you choose. This of course makes playing as any race other than caucasian, somewhat immersion breaking, but this may come to change; it seems the developers are certainly not finished polishing the game, so to expect more to come is fair at this point.
Visually, the game is stunning. It takes an old and tasteful gameplay style and throws great graphics into the mix for an experience that makes you want to explore every inch of the world. Every detail is thoroughly implemented, not only on visual levels, but can also affect your gameplay! One of the game's selling points is the ability to combine environmental elements for reactive results. For example, if it's raining, chances are everyone gets wet, which makes them easier to freeze with ice spells, or stun with electricity. It also forms puddles on the ground, which can be shocked to form a stunning field, locking everyone who touches it in place for a few turns. Even impressively intricate combinations can take place; douse some burning ground with water to create a steam cloud, and zap it to make a stunning storm-cloud! Just make sure you're not in the area of effect too, or else you may suffer from your own devising...
The above seems far too complicated for a real-time combat scenario, which is why the fact it's turn-based makes it a reasonable tactic. Anyone who's partaken in Dungeons & Dragons (and enjoyed it) can respect turn-based combat for what it is; giving you ample time to plot and devise your character's move, around your teammates' and enemies' own. You get 'action points' each turn, which you can spend on various abilities and actions during your phase, and reserve for the next turn if you're not quite ready, or don't have enough action points to pull off that big hit you want. This makes combat slow-ish, but with friends controlling the other characters, communicating with them what the best course of action is, and combining efforts and elements with each other to overcome your opponents, is one of the most fun experiences I've had with an RPG for a while. Outside combat is real-time however, so don't worry about those points inbetween being boring and sluggish!
Another aspect I love about the game is the loot and crafting system. The game presents a large array of base weapons and armour, and throws some random modifiers in the mix to make sure your rewards are never quite the same. Item discoveries are also random too; you can get any kind of item anywhere, no matter if you grabbed it from a loot chest, stole it from a town-house or picked it right from someone's pocket. The crafting system is huge and diverse; you can literally craft anything from the start of the game provided you have a high enough crafting level, and know the recipe. You can find recipe books dotted around town that will give you hints as how to make this and that, but they are not required to unlock any crafting you want to do.
At the time of writing this review, the maximum amount of players is 2. You can pick up a couple of followers in town to match that party up to 4, but officially only 2 players can actively be in a game session. There is a 4-player mod, that requires two additional players to take over the two additional followers, but the mod is so glitchy and crash-prone for myself, I've chosen to give up on it. Why? The developers have openly stated that they're finishing up the official 4-player mode, they're just not ready to release it until it's properly polished. I would rather wait for this release before attempting to play with more than one other person, and avoid crashing and losing save files, altogether. The combat is just too difficult and time-consuming to humour losing progress through battles as anything but a waste, especially if the battle went well and with little cost.
Overall, if you're a big fan of Dungeons & Dragons, and you've enjoyed games like Torchlight or Diablo, you ought to give this a shot. This is as close as you get to video-game D&D without actually playing D&D. There's literally hours upon hours of content if you want to get everything out of the game, but if I could suggest anything, make sure you're in-call with the person you're playing with; communication is important in this kind of game.
Addendum: With the release of the game's Engine development tool, users can create their own campaigns and mods with relative ease. Expect to see a lot more content from the game's more creative players, especially when the Steam Workshop gets opened for it!

A good JRPG to play over a weekend. It's relatively short as JRPGs go but feels neither rushed nor padded out. The story, while hardly original, is good enough to propel things along. There is a good sense of humor buried just beneath the surface -- you don't get much of it if you just stick to the main quest without deviation, but try doing off-the-wall stuff and a lot of time the results will be pretty funny. Combat is quick and doesn't get stale, and there's a good variety of boss fights, some of them quite difficult even if you've leveled up.

Like all good CPRGs, expect to enjoy hours and hours fighting and exploring and thinking (20+ hours not shown). D:OS can be compared to other classic CRPGs, such as Balder's Gate 2 & Fallout 2, and hold its head high. i.e. It is a topdown isometric squad(?) RPG real-time then turn-based in combat. Similar to the Fallout series in that you can roam and explore and do as you like - until you get to dungeon-like instances. There will be some hard puzzle solving.
The Elemental Magic system is something the old school CRPGs dream of. eg. Water + Cold = freezing (with all the 3D animations for it). However, after you slip 3 times in a row on the same puddle of icey water (left over from the battle), you do get frustrated (until you hit level 10 and get the tornado spell).
In D:OS you have everything you would expect from a CRPG - stealing from NPCs, bartering, lock picking, quicksave-scumming on traps. >.> Also like old school CRPGs, the battles will seem very hard until you understand the strategy - especially for the boss fights. Pro Tip: items and gold is common, XP is a limited commodity.
The dialogue is funny, quirky and numerous. Character ratings (like-ability) unfortunately has no real consequence. The dialogue is also competitive when deciding which AI or Human character is the winner of the dialogue options. This is done with Rock-Paper-Scissors with skills influencing points won. It makes perfect sense for a RPG with skill-checks, especially with multiplayer. FWIW - co-op is absolutely awesome (but it is difficult to find a friend I know who plays CRPGs, sigh).
The Unity engine is a mixed blessing. There is a an editor (creating levels and whatever), "mod-ability" is very high. Graphics are good but nothing amazing. D:OS could have been a 10/10 game if released on a custom CRPG engine top graphics. There are still a few bugs in game but nothing game breaking (I expect they will all be fixed within a month or two of this review).
I backed D:OS on Kickstarter and played the beta as well. You are not missing out on anything if you get the DLC - except for a discount. Highly recommend.

Divinity: Original Sin is the latest entry in the Divinity series of games, chronologically following Divinity: Dragon Commander and preceeding the events of Divine Divinity.  It is also an unbelievably good game and you should play it immediately.
Maybe I should explain.
Original Sin chronicles the tale of two Source Hunters, inquisitorial figures who have been granted vast authority by the Council of Seven, as they travel the world of Rivellon.  The premise is well-trod in other games; crusaders questing to destroy dark Sourcerers, who must face dire threats while keeping themselves from becoming the very monsters they yadda yadda yadda.
But this is a Divinity game.  This is the direct sequel to the game wherein you played an army commander who was also a dragon wearing a jetpack.
Rivellon is an incredible world to explore- one part hilarious, one part tragic, two parts engrossing.  After you've made your way through the tomb which serves as a tutorial, the game world is simply open, the tasks blinking in your journal neither pushing nor pulling.  In our playthrough, my friend and I have found ourselves moving through the world like water; taking the most interesting paths of least resistance and criss-crossing the map in crazed fashion.  Against the backdrop of a town Councillor's murder, we helped a cat find love, or fought the ghosts of pirates, or battled our way slowly through a monsterous hellscape on a whim.  Every screen has something noteworthy taking place on it, even if it's not immediately obvious what,  and NPC conversations, dialogue, environmental cues and short in-game books are meshed seamlessly into a dramatic and intriguing whole.
As far as the cliche-sounding plotline goes, the story may surprise you.  Nearly as soon as the mundane primary quests begin, they are interwoven with a metaplot on a cosmic level- but they remain fulfilling and well-done stories.  Every named character has a tale, and many of them are well-developed and emotional enough to give you an unusual sense of connection to the character.  After a few hours into the story, the game washes its hands of any responsibility it has to give you moral cues, and it pulls no punches with the complexity of the situations you're forced to resolve on a whim.  Lives and fortunes often depend upon a moment's indecision, and entire populations can be decimated due to a loss at rock-paper-scissors.
(I did remind you that this was a Divinity game.  How else would you resolve social conflicts?)
It might be more helpful to think of Divinity: Original Sin as a complex and interwoven series of events rather than a quest.  Most of the situations throughout the world are resolvable through several vectors, and the whole narrative can shift and adapt as you resolve things 'out of order' or shank a hapless character who caught you pawing through their storeroom.  Plots and schedules in the game world exist with some degree of independance- so when I accidentally set a fishing boat on fire and was forced to slay all of the enraged dockworkers, I cut away the thread which would have led me to the location of the mutineer who'd stolen a valuable artifact... but I came across him later anyway.
Speaking of killing, combat in this game is interesting in a way I've seldom seen before.  Proper fights are turn-based, and unbelievably dynamic and well-balanced.  No abilities are lost on the live-time overworld, however, and so encounters can be started after hurling a fireball at an unwitting group, or re-arranging the scenery to form barricades.  Fights are dangerous affairs- the game does not beleive in pulling punches, and being outnumbered is a threat which must be countered with cunning tactics and even emergant changes of planning.
No more dangerous than the world itself, though.  Rivellon is riddled with traps, puzzles and (well) riddles, and a lapse in attention can mean the death of even an over-levelled party.  Death is a serious matter- ressurection scrolls are real, but rare, and even those won't help you if your entire party goes up in flames.  This is a key element of the game; that the things happening on-screen are things you have to pay attention to, lest you walk blithely into the basement of a paranoid trap-maker or idly break a barrel full of oil while an open fire is alight nearby.
Finally, the multiplayer element is excellent.  While (by default, anyway) only two people can play the same game, each one has full control over a character, and frequent opportunities for choices by each player helps to tailor the character to fit both desires.  The game's plot is built with a dual protagonist in mind, and teamwork is absolutely required in even the most routine battles.  Best of all, the game's interconnectivity system allows players to swap items or teleport to the other in a flash, giving each hero freedom to wander the world map while retaining the ability to show up and participate in combat.
Are there problems with this game?  Of course, but they're blessedly minor.  The game has a few more bugs than you might expect, and load times between areas are long.  It's also easy to skip side-quests, and some of the more important ones contain puzzles sufficiently obscure to create serious problems for some players- plus, though the game lets you do what you want and ignore what you don't, skipping the wrong side-quests can cause serious problems later on.  Finally, the game's NPCs have a solid reprotoire of relevant and witty dialog... which they will repeat, ad infinitum.  This can quickly come to grate on the senses, and I have legitimately killed NPCs merely to make them shut up.
Still, these substantive quibbles are minor.  Divinity: Original Sin, is one of the most solid RPG titles which I've seen in years, and more fun to boot.

This is going to be a review of great length, of mixed feelings, of ups and downs, and of hopefulness. It will go chronologically from the beginning to the end (at the time of posting) of my experience with the game.
First off, I have snowboarded for a good portion of my life. I started more than 5 years ago and have loved it ever since. I've snowboarded in Utah and Colorado every year since I first experience how fun winter sports are. In terms of this game, I've played it during two of its private testing phases, as well as the final public testing phase. Although I only have 11 hours in the game at this time, in reality I have played steep more than double that amount of time. I have gold-medaled almost every challenge on almost every mountain except the Matterhorn and Mont Blanc, and you will soon discover why this is the case. Originally I intended on reviewing this game after gold-medaling all of the challenges, but I was tomahawking down the Matterhorn when I realized that it was time.
Now, to the review.
The tutorial is fine. Having played the game before, I was annoyed that it was mandatory, but it ended with relative swiftness and I was able to be on my way. It was useful for the uninformed, and fast enough not to discourage those that know what they're up to. The first locations I played around in were the lower mountains. These are my favorite places to play this game. The physics and controls (ironically) work best in areas of less steep terrain. The game is relaxing, the lighting is beautiful, and it's a playground for skiing and snowboarding. PIllow fields are fun to jump around in, there are alpine forests to hike through on foot or shoot through on snowboard/skis. Around the peaks you can find wonderful routes to paraglide, and you can wingsuit through trees and powerlines for an adrenaline rush. There are plenty of cliffs to ski down and plenty of rooftops to jump off of. I even managed to jib a tree, which honestly might be my personal favorite accomplishment so far in my experience with the game. I love the lower mountains because they are enjoyable.
After sufficiently leveling up to gain access to the more "challenging" (but in actuality more frustrating) mountains, I had my foray in those as well. Peak of the damned was difficult, but I enjoyed myself for the most part. I damned some of the challenges for reasons I will soon mention. One of my first (minor) gripes with this game was noticed here. Some of the challenges you do reset your ambiance (basically, the lighting and mood of the game world) to what seems to be a predetermined mode. This is annoying and cannot be tampered with. Giving the player the power to change the ambiance of the game and then wresting that control from them at certain points in the game is something I would like to be able to opt out of.
The Matterhorn is where my feelings for this game take a turn. The Matterhorn is the epitome of the difference between something that is HARD and something that is CHALLENGING. Peak of the Damned was challenging for me. I had plenty of goes at the challenges before I got gold, but I never felt like they were impossible (save one challenge that, in hindsight, was foreshadowing of what was to come). On the other hand (or ski), the Matterhorn was simply hard. The challenges given to you are nigh-impossible. I don't say that because I couldn't do them. I gold-medaled a good portion of them; however, I did so after crashing over and over, hiking up the mountain to reach checkpoints, and skiing down when I could.
The Matterhorn is supposed to be extreme, but I don't believe it's designed to frustrate you. I don't believe it would frustrate you if the game played as the game should play. Ah, the meat and potatoes of the argument. The game does not function as it should.
Rocks are like lava. If you run into a rock going 40 mph, of course you should crumble. That's realistic. What isn't realistic (and is instead extremely frustrating) is wiping out because you skiied over a 15 foot stretch of smooth rock/ice on the face of a mountain, and your knees gave out like they were remotely detonated.
Switching direction of travel requires two thumbsticks to be pushed in opposite directions. Why is it, then, that as I slide down the side of the Matterhorn Jeremy-Jones style so as not to crash, with the left thumbstick pointing back and the right thumbstick untouched, that my rider decides to change direction?
Winguiting is fun as all hell. Nothing is wrong with it.
Paragliding is fun as all hell. Nothing is wrong with it.
I'm sure I could play another hour of the game and encounter more of my forgotten gripes with this game, but I think I've made a point. The game has SO much potential. It's already the best game on PC that has ever been made in the snowsports genre. If the phyics are fixed, the G-force system is rewired, and unrealistic ways of dealing with real-world occurences are done away with, this game will kick♥♥♥♥♥ I'll still be playing the game after this review is published, but I'm going to spend a lot less time on the more harsh mountains. They would be fun if the game was built to handle them, but untill all of the game mechanics are fixed to allow CHALLENGING descents on the harsher mountains, not FRUSTRATING ones, I'll be spending my time cruising through some low-elevation powder.
If there's anything in this review that I seem to have missed and/or totally screwed up on, please notify me so I can take care of it.
TL;DR: If you want to cruise through powder, fly adrenaline-pumping wingsuit routes, and enjoy the beauty of the mountains, buy the game on sale. It's the best there is at the moment. If you're looking to descend mountains that no one would descend in real life, I wouldn't recommend it. You won't want to descend them in-game either.

Knights of Pen & Paper, originally for iOS, is a turn-based RPG with a novel concept: you take on the role of real-life players in a tabletop game.  The camera is set behind a table where up to five of your characters are seated, with the dungeon master on the other side leading you through the story.  Dialogue tends to be humorous and frequently goes out of character.
The game begins with character creation, where you must assign your players a real-life persona and one of a dozen traditional RPG classes, each with four skills.  The actual gameplay takes place around your table, as if you’re in the middle of all the action, and consists of traveling to locations on a world map and completing quests, which are really just more battles in disguise.  In fact, the entire game is simply one battle after another and becomes very repetitive, very fast.
As expected, level-ups provide stat bonuses and allow you to upgrade your skills and wear better equipment.  Armor and weapons may only be improved at the blacksmith, but each character has four additional slots for equipping various accessories.  In addition to in-game shops, there is a “real-life” shop where you may purchase snacks that provide temporary buffs for your players, as well as decorations and furniture that confer permanent bonuses.
Overall, Knights of Pen & Paper is passable in the context of mobile gaming but completely forgettable when compared to quality games on the PC platform.  Considering the price is $9.99 on Steam vs a mere $2.99 on iOS and Android, it’s borderline offensive that the devs left in-app purchases in the game, allowing you to buy gold with your Steam wallet funds.  Such a shameless exhibit of its mobile origins is a fitting red flag for a game that also fails to break away from the shallow, repetitive gameplay those origins typically entail.

In all the ways a game utilizes already established forms of art, the Banner Saga excels.  The visuals are stunning in their detail, beauty, and style evoking the legacy of Eyvind Earle.  The music evokes the mood and setting quite deftly.  The narrative itself perfectly balances world-threatening-menace endemic to fantasy storytelling and more intimate plotlines focusing around the theme of family.
Mechanically the game is novel.  The complexity of the combat emerges from simple mechanics, and (refreshingly) cannot be gamed by grinding.  In this way I would say that the experience of combat is well curated.
There are also larger scale 'war' battles.  These consist of giving the size of the respective forces, and letting the character pick from a variety of tactical options.  Most of these options (i.e., 'charge,' 'formations,' etc) result in playing out a regular battle with the option to go a second round to earn greater rewards.  The biggest flaw in this aspect of the game is that it isn't made particularly clear what effect the various options actually have.
The other mechanical aspect of the game involves managing a caravan of refugees as they treck agross the games gorgeously detailed world.  This basically involves managing food by purchasing it in town and gaining (or losing) it in events in the world and managing morale by deciding when to make camp and rest.  Most of the events in the game are sort of choose-your-own-adventure dialogue puzzles.  Unlike, say, BioWare games there are definitely wrong answers in dialogue and saying or doing the wrong thing can result in losing valuable party members or resources.
The pacing of the game is slow and plodding, but for me this actually added to the experience.  The pacing evokes the slog, misery, and dread that must be experienced by the Banner Saga's Protagonists.
The Banner Saga has my hearty recommendation.

This review is for the game ''Shadowgrounds''.
Developer:Frozenbyte
Release dates:Windows: November 11, 2005 (Finland, Germany)
Linux:September 16, 2009,Mac OS X:April 13, 2011,Steam:May 8, 2006
Genre:Single player,local co-op top-down shooter(shoot em up)
Recap
There's not much to tell since it's a really straightforward game.The plot is really simple-some would say cliché- about Wesley Tyler, a senior mechanic on the IGTO Repair Base on Jupiter's satellite Ganymede,whose responsibility is to repair various systems.During his work he finds some dead bodies,then finds a pistol and other forms of weaponry and -oh the irony- alliens begin to invade the planet(in this case the satellite).You have to progress through 11 levels,save some troopers,destroy some engines and kill many(many many many) hostile aliens.In the end(spoiler alert) you will find out that the aliens really weren't that bad,though they had fallen victims to their own greed and destroyed their own home planet and most of their own race with that kind of technology.That's why they've been monitoring the human race and when they found out they would use that kind of energy.Our hero and his friends decide to give the AMEW bomb back and save eventually the entire solar system(surprising right?)
Pros: 1)Simple yet enjoyable story,2)Pleasant time consuming(and yes that's a pro for me),3)Fairly cheap
Cons:1)Limited, no-brainer skill costumization,2)Not much of a challenge(aliens and alien bosses are really easy even at the hardest difficulty,3)Lame voice acting and some of the lamest quotes in gaming.
Overall a nice pleasant time consuming game.I recommend this game but not for the people who need a challenge though.
Thank you Frozenbyte Developers for this game :).

Great music, amazing art style, and brilliant story-driven gameplay. Its not a game I would usually choose to play, but the survival element and migration aspect was very appealing. You really get a sense that the land and everyone in it are experiencing a great calamity and with the encounters you experience on your journey, there is a sense of urgency and survival.
My complaints are the length of the game and the price. The game is pretty short, and you think you can level up more characters before the end but thats not the case, I ended up with medium level characters for the last boss because I spread the points a bit to liberally. I had focused on a few characters, but replaying a new game you know you can ditch and forget some characters over others, mainly picking characters for their ability over anything else.
The game does have replay value, and its fun to know what you will do next time knowing what happens, but after that your only left with multiplayer, or maybe replaying it to find out alternatives to minor narratives along the game. The current price is a bit much, but not too far from what I would expect to pay for a quality (if not short) game like this.
Its a very good game, and very enjoyable and does a great job at sucking you into the world (wait till you see the map, all that lore!). Hopefully Stoic will make the next game in this trilogy a bit longer, but apart from that its a winning gameplay formula and style.

Good:
- Combat is fun. It's a dynamic system where you can chain effects or use surrounding objects in a fight (e.g. throw a nearby candle onto an oil slick and light enemies on fire).
- Co-op. You can play +1 other person, which I appreciate.
- Sneaking around and stealing everyone's stuff is pretty dang funny. So many hams.
- Buffs & stats based on your character's moral decisions make you delve into some cool character alignment choices.
Needs Improvement:
- Quest tracking system. There's no quest tracking other than manually opening your journal and reading through. All the quests pile up, and some are quite long, so you end up just spamming conversation with NPCs in hopes it will solve a quest for you.
- Multiplayer dialog. When you play with someone else and they open up dialog with an NPC, you cannot see what they are saying, or conversation options they choose. Unless you are reading the bottom right chat window as the dialog whizzes by at blinding speeds.
- Pacing. You fight a bit, then enter the first town where you spend five hours just doing non-combat quests. It felt like I spent a whole day doing nothing.
- Character interaction. I was really hoping for more dynamic interactions between party members. Sometimes you get a few tidbits of conversation, but it all feels like you are talking to an NPC, not developing a relationship.
- Tiling options for combat system would be nice, but that's probably just a personal preference.
Why the "Not Recommended?"
I would only recommend this game if you're looking for a co-op strategic RPG. For single player, I would prefer to just play through one of the classic RPGs again (Dragon Age, KOTOR, Fallout, etc.).
