Probably my favourite puzzle game ever.
What's so special about the game is that it actually messes with your mind, rather than only trying to do so.
The puzzles are incredibly well designed and never feel unfair, while they are still challenging.
Whenever you get stuck at a certain puzzle, you can take a step back and try clearing another room.
Essentially this means it is unlikely to really get stuck somewhere, because you can simply walk away.
This pretty much keeps the game at a reasonably high pace, at least for what it is.
The only downside in my opinion, is that the final series of rooms get incredibly easy once you have unlocked the red gun.
This made the final parts feel a bit anticlimactic, rather than a puzzle in which all your gained knowledge has to be used.
All things considered, I would give this game 9/10.
If you are at least mildly interested after watching the trailer, you won't be disappointed.

When I heard about Steep, I thought it sounded like a great idea for a game but there would be no way it would be done right or hold my attention. I'm happy to say my speculation was drasticly wrong.
While it doesn't hold your hand to get started, the first few missions are relatively easy to identify and give you just enough information to continue your exploration. You only need to be mildly curious to start your adventure into the vast playable area of the Alps. The more you play, the more curious you will get. This map has a ton to offer and is bafflingly huge. Seriously, zoom in on yourself on the map and slowly zoom out. Your mind will be blown.
Among the things to do in this game are, snowboarding, skiing, paragliding, and windsuiting. Within each of these sports, there are many different types of challenges. From racing, to freestyle, to finess manuevering in the snowboarding and skiing sports, to skydiving, proximity racing and stunt racing in the windsuiting, there is plenty to keep you interested. Paragliding features racing, but where it really shines is when you use it to explore the mountain, peacefully taking in the breathtaking scenery. It truly is a beautiful world.
All of these things are at your fingertips at anytime. UI and the map allow you to seamlessly teleport to any discovered point at anytime and use whatever equipment you want from any point on the map.
Technically, the game has been supurb for me. I play at 2x hdr on my 2560x1080 monitor will max settings and Multisample AA off. I also upped the pixel multipler to 110%.
One con of the game, and this is just a personal thing, is that i can't directly share replays from the game to social media. I'd like to see this feature added in the future.

I have an old PC - 2011 I believe - with an FX-8100 CPU and an upgraded AMD R270 (an ok GPU).  I can't upgrade the GPU anymore because the motherboard is too old, so I am trying to squeeze whatever life I still can out of this rig for gaming.  I can play games like Sniper Elite 4 (2017) with no lag, so this is still a decent setup.  I experience the greatest lags on Total War games, and they come with a benchmark test so I tested this software on two games I play regularily.
Total War: Rome 2 - without CPU Cores avg 49 FPS, lowest was 25 FPS during active battle sequence.
Total War: Rome 2 - with CPU Cores - Avg 54 FPS, lowest was 32 FPS during active battle sequence
The difference of 5 FPS isn't overwhelmng, but while the game was at it's slowest it ran at 34 FPS with CPU Cores vs 24-25 FFPS without CPU cores - a valuable difference.
Next I tried Total War: Warhammer (2016) - a game that is MUCH better optimized for the current generation of multi-core chips, including my own ancient 8 core FX 8100.
TW: Warhammer without CPU Cores - 37.1 FPS
TW: Warhammer with CPU Cores - 37.4 FPS
There was very little difference between these two benchmarks.   I can see that Skyrim Special Edition with a ton of mods seems to run nicely with CPU Cores, but I have not attempted a benchmark.
Conclusion - this program works, but it's value increases when you are talking about older machines running older games.  Newer games, based on this ONE test anyway, seem to be optimized in such a fashion that they may not benifit as much from this software.  Also, more powerful CPU's may amplify the effects of this software - a 15-20 increase in FPS might be possible with a newer generation of CPU than my own...  Finally, the benifit of this software seems to be at it's greatest when the game slows down, and I would much rather have 32-34 FPS than 24-25 FPS during a big Total War battle.
My next test will be to see if CPU Cores helps my daughter's new but super cheap laptop run Sims 3 and Goat simulator faster - this might be a really helpful program for low end computers with integrated graphics.  I got this at 50% off, and at $7.50 I would say it's worth the money for me!

While not without its flaws, this has to be my favorite game of all time.  The game puts you in charge of XOM, a shadowy paramilitary group defending the earth from a mysterious alien threat.  To do this, you must amass alien technology, build your base's infrastructure, and keep the nations funding your group happy and secure.  The game is divided into two parts, first of which is a rescourse and time management game where you build your base, manage your soldiers, launch alien detecting satellites, and send your interceptors and troops out to interrupt the alien menace.
The other half is on the ground, commanding individual soldiers in turn based combat against the aliens.  Your soldiers are broken into four classes - sniper, heavy, assault, and support.  To defeat the aliens you must carefully manuever your forces in cover and execute flanking manuevers.  Since the game has embraced perma-death the danger to your soldiers seems very real, especially if you are creepy and name them after your friends, like I did.  This mechanic of high risk combat and permanent death leads to the game creating interesting stories, I am pretty sure I texted a friend thanks after he saved the entire squad with a lucky critical hit.
While the game does not have much of a story, Enemy Unknown beautifully executes tone.  There is a constant danger to your soldiers, and when new aliens pop up I always got the feeling of meeting the licker for the first time in Resident Evil.   There is also a wonderful hint of moral ambiguity when interrogating aliens and developing their technology.  It is just under the surface, and I have seen few games nail subtext.  Unless, of course, you have the Enemy Within expansion in which case the game is all WHO ARE WE TO PLAY GOD?!?!@!1 (but it also gives you 12 foot tall mec soldiers and camo skin, so who gives a fart).
I'm no Desert Fox, so playing through on Classic Ironman (with more than a few restarts) was one of most tense and rewarding experiences I have had in gaming.  That said, the game is not without a few flaws:  It has a bit of a learning curve, especially if you want to play on ironman which I believe the developers intended.  By its nature, once you learn the alien's technology the game can actually get easy and repetitive by the end.  Finally, its easy to fall into slow, cautious, turtling tactics which aren't as fun to play, but rewarded by the game.  The Enemy Within expansion ameliorated this slightly with the addition of Meld, but I felt it was a band-aid.  That said, I think this game is worth playing for anyone and essential for any fan of squad strategy games.

Dying light is a very good game and I would highly recommend picking it up at some point.
-----Pros-----
Graphics - The game generally looked very good even on low settings, textures, lighting, models etc etc were well above what I was expecting
Optimization - playing on a laptop with 2.4ghz i7 and gtx 860m, the game was fine with almost no hick ups while on low and medium settings, and as i said before the game looked great while doing so
World Design - The levels in the game are designed for parkour, there is a lot of verticallity and complexity to the buildings and layouts. The world feels really good to explore in.
Movement - The parkour system is well done and easy to use. It feels rewarding to jump off zombies heads and slide under gates. works well both with keyboard and mouse and a controller.
Combat - the combat system is pretty expansive for a first person game featuring many different types of attacks. jumping attacks, grappling, ground slams, spinning moves. my only beef with the combat is that you can't block without a shield while human NPCs can. You are provided with a grapple and many other evasive manuevers in it's place though.
Interface - The games menues and HUD are well designed, information is provided at a glance.
Multiplayer - This is where the game really shines. Dying light is definitely one of the best current gen multiplayer games, almost full campaign coop besides the intro and the very last end mission. connecting to a game is easy, and in game connections are stable. the game also offers asymmetric pvp which looks really good but i haven't had the chance to try it yet. Only beef with the coop is your partner needs to be practically standing on your head before you can initiate dialogue with anyone.
DLC - The base game is good, and they are continuing to release solid content for it.
-----Cons-----
Difficulty curve- The game starts out very difficult, zombies take forever to kill and it really forces you to play stealthily and avoid confrontation to get things done. Once you start leveling things begin to change, weapon dmg goes through the roof and you are given many executes to finish off zombies in one or two hits.
NG+ and hard mode - I was dissapointed when i loaded into new game plus and switched the difficulty to hard mode hoping the game would take a massive difficulty boost. Zombies hurt more but they were still very easy to kill and avoid. It lacked that panicky feeling that was so prevelent in the first few hours of the game.
Weapon degredation - weapon degredation is crazy in this game, even more so than fallout and dead island. The part that really gets to me is the fact that you can't repair a weapon forever, it eventually needs to get referbished. I found only a single referbishing quest on my first play through.
Story - bland, love interest is really forced and awkward. connections to other characters seem superficial. The bad guy is cartoonishly evil and hard to relate to. Not so bad that the story takes away from the amazing gameplay.
Side missions - I have mixed feelings about the side missions although they were somewhat bland fetch quests you do meet the most interesting characters in these missions and your interactions with them develops a solid feeling for the world. Although the goal was pick 5 mushrooms or gather the gasoline or whatever it often brought you to interesting places and made you interact with puzzles in a way that you would not have had to with the story. If you enjoyed side quests in skyrim and fallout you would probably like these.

Alright, this game is amazing in a way that I can honestly say I haven't really come across before.
It is also brutal, annoying, and at times depressing, but this is in part why it is so amazing.  Most games that offer you some kind of choice make it clear what the result of your choices are going to be, and even if they don't, there are often multiple ways around the problem (save scumming or similar tactics).  Banner Saga fights that trend, both with its save system, but also, and perhaps more importantly, by separating the consequenecs of your choices from the moment in which you make the choice.  Honestly, at times, it feels almost like you are one of the Starks in the Game of Thrones, with people dying without you having much control over it, but this is why the game is SO GOOD.  It gives you power to affect the story, but it doesn't make that story happy, easy, and most importantly, it doesn't make it simple.
This is the kind of game I want to see more of, something that doesn't hold the hand of the player, a game that can actually make me feel base on MY decisions.
Oh, and just for the record, the art is awesome, the combat is deceptively simple (look close enough and there is a TON of depth), but for me, it is that journey, that awesome bane of my existence for the last however many hours, that really makes this game.
Go play it, now.

Through its amazingly beautiful artworks, The Banner Saga unfolds its story before your eyes like a good book: It doesn't explain you everything firsthand, or spoil its world with "explanations for dummies" of why this story and where is what.
No, it treats you as an intelligent reader (rather, gamer) and only leads you by hints, letting your imagination to fill the gaps between the narrative, like in a proper novel. Although you are not quite sure where the story is going, you know it's epic, desperate, and at the same time, contains enough rays of hope that let you long for your characters to reach peace and a better day.
True, from a pure gaming perspective, although clever, its mechanics stay very simple, and could be seen as repetitive. But you don't want to win every battle out of cleverness, to "beat the game". You want to win them so that maybe, hopefully, this will save more of your clansmen, fighters and varls. Because the story infuses you with empathy for its likeable and complex characters, offers you few but tough choices, you end up really carring for them, not because you have level them up, but because of who they are: Rook, Alette, Iver, and all the others, struggling to survive, being doubtfull about their (yours !) decisions, hoping they will reach a happy ending.
The Banner Saga is quite a unique game, because it manages something very hard to reach with this media: It conveys emotions.
I can understand it's not a journey for everyone, but it definitely transported me...

What an unbeliveably bad game. I bought this for around three euros in the sales and I still feel short-changed.
It's one of those games that's difficult simply for the sake of being difficult. You can tell that the designers just ran out of ideas on how to make the game properly challenging and just jacked the difficulty curve up. This game is set up to annoy and frustrate the player, the random teleporting suicide squads who came out of no-where (from no ship) were a prime example of this.
It's a game for those who think that difficulty is the same as (or a good substitute for) a challenging task, in other words, morons. It was pitched to me by a friend who said: "You can play it perfectly and STILL lose!", when I asked him how on earth that could constitute into a good game he just told me "I didn't get it", and he's right I don't get the whole "Dying the part of the fun!" bit. No; Dying is not fun in a game! Especially not when I've been playing for a good hour and It gets dropped on me that I've to kill the final boss three times! (or more, i don't know, as I'm not bothering with this crap anymore)
It's a game that encourages you to grind through the levels (their words exactly) even though the constant dying means any items you get will be gone at the restart. There very little variety in the action, after a few hours you'll have encountered most of the scenarios you're ever going to. It VERY quickly gets really boring. Soon you'll be able to spot the points where you know you don't have a chance if the game progresses and you'll end up just hitting restart rather then try and grind a decent item for the next half hour only to just die anyway.
What really annoys me is that this game really could've been great, if they'd just added more variety and toned down the stupid difficulty level. This really could've one of those games that takes years off your life and you loving it.
If you are one of those weirdos who loved Dark Souls simply because the game was impossible to beat and that's what kept you grinding through it like water torture then this is the game for you. If you're sane and/or have taste save yourself time and use the money to buy a girl you like a coffee. Even if you crash and burn it'll give you more of a thrill than this game.....

Quick Review and Tips (+ high res fix) for new players :
Since game features are listed above , no need going through them here . In short , this is a rougelike shooter with with an old vampire movie setting . It is a on-the-toes game that makes sure to keep you on the go as your health remains low while danger lurks at every dark corner . Thanks to the random castle generation (mostly interor of the castle , some locations remain fixed) every replay tends to be different . It's like 2016 Doom but retro style type of gameplay . The music is simply incredible . Amazing vampiric ambience , especialy in the tower . If you like vampire themes , then this is as much as one can get , stakes , coffins , crucifix . It's all in there .
Tips :
- First of all download high detail and wide res fix here :
- There is no inventory . If you pick up a health pack , it is applied right away . Any used above 100 hp will only grant temporary hp points .
- Don't forget that a stake can become a torch . Helps in the dark places .
- The number next to your items is how many of them you own . Meaning you might have 3-4 guns . People think that there is a glitch with the number of bullets displayed , but it fact the game cycles through the guns you own , each with it's own equipped bullet count . Feel free to reload each gun and then switch from one to another when you fire . It's very effective .
- One of the relatives can give you a key to save the dog .
- Some weapons have alt fire with the right click .
- Dialog that shows up when you save a relative actually pauses the game despite the sound . Feel free to take your time and read .
- Your relatives will not follow you if there is danger ahead . They will wait for you to finish your fight and you can tell them to come along when it's safe again . Careful with weapons near the relatives , especially guns and stakes .
- The sound plays a big role in this game . It will warn you when something is about to strike you down , so use it to your advantage . (Especially music)
- Losing a relative is not the end of the game . It's more on "save as many as you can" . The final boss gains power with each relative lost . You can lose a total of 6 (or 5 , can't recall properly).
- There is a bug that crashes the game sometimes when you encounter the final boss . Restarting the game tends to fix it . Also that rumor that the last two relatives cannot be saved seems to be fake as I saved them each time I played .
- If you leave your dog behind , it will return to the doghouse in the courtyard . (If he survives the trip)
If you are unsure about getting this game , then feel free to try the demo version that features a random generated third floor of the west wing and a boss battle . Link :

Nosferatu is a janky old game, but it's still not enough jank to ruin the experience, though it would be great to have a remaster to fix the bugs.
Nosferatu has you play a dude whose family foolishly thought to marry their daughter to the creepy corpse-looking dude that lives in a desolate Transylvanian castle that's totally legit and not a vampire so now you got to save them. The game happens in real time so if you don't hurry your family members can die, said time limit isn't that restrictive though and escorting your family members is actually not bad because they're competent enough at following you and enemies will gun for you most of the time. Nosferatu: The Wrath of Malachi is a good, intense, Classic horror game. It’s got a good bit of problems, but it’s still good. Now for the story.
You play as James Patterson a man from a poor, but proud, aristocratic family of the British nobility. He is on his way to the wedding of his sister, Rebecca, at Castle Malachi, where she is to be wed to the son of the wealthy Romanian Count.
But as soon as he gets there, he sees that his family and friends luggage are abounded, and crosses nailed to the castle's door. What happened, where are his family and their friends, it’s up to him to find out.
What I liked about this game. I liked the old Gothic Castle. The creepy and intense atmosphere, the monsters were scary too, like the Foul Beast Vampire Boss you fight.
Now like I said the game has a bit of problems. First, you see in the game you need to save your family and friends before they are killed and sacrificed, but the AI for them was a little bad like getting stuck or getting in the way of killing monsters, or just walking off a high pleas and dying.
Hell all most the whole game is a bit buggy, but not game braking. Now for the bosses. They are okay easy to kill, but wish they a bit more unique the only one who were unique, is the Foul Beast Vampire Boss. Then there is the last boss witch was a little disappointing.
But with all that said I liked game. And like I said with some other older game I think remake of this would be good. You can get this game for $9.99 but I say wait till it’s on sale. So if you want to play some good old school horror games, this one is a good start

I bought this for 0,99$ during sale and as much as it had few funny and entertaining moments,
I don't recommend this game and here's why:
Nosferatu is the first person shooter where you have to find and rescue bunch of NPC's randomly hidden all around the castle.
Some of NPC's can be slain before even finding them due time limit, but saving all of them is not required to finish the game itself.
You search for keys to access new areas and rescue NPC's for additional rewards such as items with passive bonus or new weapons. After finding/slain all of available NPC's, dawn starts and you can acces the final boss fight on top of the castle.
The main idea of this game is randomization of items, NPC's and enemies (yet locations, rooms and overall game progression stays the same) but randomization is in real time which means you can just save/reload save state to re-roll what is inside of room (items, enemies, NPC's) and chest reward (before you gonna open them) kinda ruining whole idea.
There is no any sort of in-game map and area layout is just beyond confusing. West Wing and bottom of the Castle are simple enough but East Wing and rest of the castle is gonna give you a headache. Not to mention that this game have way, way too many copy paste rooms with addition of auto closing doors behind you will make it even harder to remember what rooms you did already visit.
Game engine is really broken. Visual bugs, flickering textures and weird artifacts all over this game, prerendered cutscenes, getting stuck on every objects, you slide on floor like on ice, sometimes even bounce of from stairs, walls and chests makes yout take fall damage quite often. This also applies to NPC's, which may couse their death at random point. Sometimes NPC may die for just standing still or if you move to far away from them. Quite often I died for no reason by just entering room and I still don't know why or how.
Enemies can spawn when you revisit rooms, even behind you or on your eyes - getting even more cheap hits on you. Doors are closing itself constantly blocking enemies, allies or you. Heck, opening doors can even kill you at max health. Just instant death from being squashed by them at random points due engine error. Broken UI, mouse wheel changes weapon very slowly makes combat even more difficult. It will even sometimes say wrong number of ammo.
Game mechanics are just beyond terrible: weapon reload sometimes work, sometimes doesn't, both enemies and ally NPC's will constatnly get stuck on everything or they will just straight block your way, sometimes forcing you to reload save state. Stamina that goes down really fast for just walking, running and melee combat may sounds like a good idea on paper but it gets annoying really fast, especially when you fight more than one enemy.
Hidden timer on life of few NPC's is forcing you to hurry up which combined with how stamina works, castle layout and game engine will give you huge, annoying problems while playing.
Also when timer will reach midnight enemies will start spawning like 3 times more often will drain your health and ammo really fast if you not hurry up.
Combat is very simple yet broken. Enemies getting cheap shots on you when fighting with melee and range, can't even run away from them to reload your one shot musket because of how stamina works.
Even weapons are broken: your first weapon available (fists) is one of the strongest weapons allowing you stunlock enemies until they die, Crucifix supposed to repel certain enemies but its sometimes work, sometimes not and Chalice is so strong that it kills any boss with one hit, including last finale boss.
You can pick up ammo and health when max yet this couse you to waste them.
Enemies and bosses deal so much damage that you will die and reload save state quite often in this game, even on easy difficulty.
You can have up to 9 save states and you can save wherever you are but loading game may couse spawn of enemies right in front of you in the room.
Overall game take less than 3 hours to finish.
Game runs on very low resolution and there is no way to change that. Actually there is no options menu so you can't even change volume of SFX or music.
Even keybinds aren't consistent as you can re-bind only half of them for some reason.
Final verdict: honestly, this game really need a proper remaster. There is some potential but it's really buried under a pile of glitches and some serious annoying problems.
In short: this game didn't age well. I do recommend playing it only to fans of very old, clunky games and only on huge discount. Definitely not worth more than 2$.

Massively over-rated game.  I don't want to be given a sandbox, and then told there's only one right way to go, which is exactly what happens in Mirror's Edge.  Creating the ILLUSION of a sandbox is worse than just creating a standard game, because you psych me up for a sandbox, I'm massively disappointed when you don't deliver it.  The story is made to sound better on the surface than it really unfolds, and you're not given enough character context to really form sympathy or attachment.  They make it look like the main lead is a very skilled hand to hand combatant, but she's quite weak, and you're often surrounded by so many enemies, especially untouchable aerial enemies, that fighting back is the furthest thing from a reasonable option.  Additionally, while I understand that this is a platformer, we're given the impression that the main character is incredibly confident and skilled at these acrobatics.  Unless you go well beyond a single play through, you will never gain the sense of confidence as a player that the character should have, which I believe is points against it.  If you're playing a badass, you should eventually come to feel like a badass.  If you're playing an expert parkour ♥♥♥♥♥, you should eventually come to feel like an expert parkour ♥♥♥♥♥.  It never happens.  If this game lived up to the ads it put out, it would have been the brilliant masterpiece that all the paid-under-the-table games media said it was.  It did not live up to any of that.  I would buy this game for $5, and not a penny more.  It's already gained far more praise and revenue than it ever deserved.  The only thing that wasn't underwhelming, when compared to what they promised to deliver, was the atmosphere.
PS-- I played this more through Origin than through steam.  I finished the game.  Certainly I've played more than 1.7 hours, but probably less than 10.

the only REAL drawback is that I finished the xcom enemy unknown game in 12 hours... a little short arc of story, because the in game videos look great and could have really have been able to give more meat to a "doomed world under siege"; also I would say there could have been more "council missions" or the actual defense of your own base when the aliens find your bunker complex (which did exit in the first three xcom games and was fun because basicaly the combat map WAS your base as you laid it out, which offered a deeper level of planning and actualy the chance to see your base in "live action" situations too when bracing for the aliens assault).
ok, the game overall? good concept, graphics and details of character movements, but the background music (it was more of a constant droning and buzzing background) seriously sucked... some "heroic" stargate like music orchestration for some intense moments could have given it a lil more kick, but for those who like scifi battles, its a good if too short game.

After just completing one playthrough I am pleased with The Banner Saga. Visually unique by its drawn artwork and backed by an amazing soundtrack makes most scenes quite interesting. While it might seem boring to watch a caravan slowly churn to the next location or waiting for the next event. I mostly just found myself drawn in. My biggest complaint, which isn't even a big one to me, is I wished more dialogue was voiced. 99% of all dialogue is text, which is fine for me to read but I'd certainly be down for Ubin (the narrator) talking more. The voice work that is there is very well done, just used sparingly.
The gameplay itself is mostly broken down into two segments, the combat itself and moving around the world. Traveling has very little options on "where to go", but some events allow for options. The system works by having renown (currency used to upgrade heroes and buy items/supplies) balanced between having enough food to not starve, but still upgrade units. Combat can stress this because having people get injured requires rest, which takes a day of supplies to do.
Ultimately it works fairly well but any nags I would have end up being drowned out by me enjoying the overall experience. It does become fairly difficult, and that was just on normal. But I bet if I replayed it I would have less issues, but I'm willing to bet hard difficulty would be a challenege.
I would definetly reccomend anyone to play this game if you enjoy turn based combat games (kings bounty, might/magic, etc) or someone who just enjoys a good world to sink yourself into.
For whats basically a 3 man made game for ~700k. I am quite content with what was released from my original backing. I am definetly looking forward to seeing chapter 2/3

Have you ever played Titan Quest, and thought that this game has potential, but it's a bit slow, the skill trees are a bit meh, there's little to do and the itemization system is not very deep? Then this game is for you. Grim Dawn is based on the Titan Quest engine, but they reworked it immensly. It's faster, it's darker and there's pretty much a solution for every concern I've listed above. The only problem is that it's still in alpha, so it's not finished.
Currently, the maximum lvl is 40, and you might think that 'so I ran trough the 2 and a half acts then what?' and it's a good question. The answer is, there's a lot to do already. Grim Dawn implements a lot of little things that makes an ARPG good:
-replayability by level scaling: if you've reached max lvl, and want to 'farm', you're not restricted to the last dungeon/boss of the game, you can run through the major areas in act1, because it's scaled up to your level, so it's won't get boring, because there's at least 10 areas currently that you can farm
-blue items without fixed stats: self explanatory, you find a blue item, there's a range of stats it can get, so there's always room for improvement
-green items with crazy stats: green items are basically the 'rares' of diablo2 but with a possibility to become much better than blues, so again, there's always room for improvement if you want to find a green item that's even better than a blue one
-components: components are item enchantments, again, with varied stats for bonuses when you complete one. All I say is, you can even get a component with a completion bonus with +1 all skills
-relics: relics are a bit hard to craft items which enhance a specific type of gameplay, difficult to craft them, but it's worth it
And there's more to come:
-weapon 'powders' from faction rewards, which enhance weapons even more, so reputation is important
-faction rewards, again, reputation
-Nemesis, or 'most hated' reputation tier which causes that more and stronger monsters will come at you or even specific bosses which are only available at this tier
Grim Dawn has a multiplayer option, which currently are not central server based, but gives a rewarding experience and generally, it's more fun to play with others.
If you are unfamilar with Titan Quest but you know Diablo 2, then I can wholeheartedly recommend this game to you, because it has everything that made Diablo 2 a classic, and it could be even more.
The review wouldn't be complete if I didn't list some negative things too, so here they are:
-it's being made by a small team, so you can't expect immediate content patches and huge updates, so you have to be patient
-there are some quirky stats and effects in the game which needs explanation, but if you read the forums, you'll understand everything

Might this be a zombie-game worth buying you might be thinking. If you like zombies, the answer is probably yes. Zombies has always been my favourite genre in videogames and about half of my games sets me in the apocalypse. This game however offered me an experience other zombiegames failed to deliver. Zombies, and parkour is a quite unique combination but works very well. The designers has achieved a great balance between kick♥♥♥♥♥zombie action and a very smooth parkour system which supports every move you make. That is probably the best thing about this game. The movement is so accurate. I will now try my best to summarize my thoughts in an original pros and cons list:
Pros
+Amazing parkour system which is difficult to find on the same level in other similar games. 9/10
+Good variety between the different zombies you will have to deal with throughout the game. You will find anything from sneaky little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s hunting you down from afar to tanky, clumpsy giants ready to smash you down. This dissables your ability to adapt and learn about the enemy as they all behave differently. Even though there is a variety, I feel like most of the ideas are very straight on copied from other developers. 7/10
+Great graphics, of course. But I have seen better. Honestly, in this type of game there should be alot more focus on gameplay, which they have succeeded with. 7/10
+Loot system is also something quite different here. I love how you have to take the risk of going out of the safesone just to get to that airdrop or that crate you spotted earlier. It makes you feel independent, and by that I mean you have to make choices, and not as the character you are playing as but yourself. Great job. 9/10
+Story is ok I guess. I haven't made it very far into the game yet (but sure do I enjoy it) and there doesn't seem to be a very deep telling about how the world got to this..♥♥♥♥♥♥ The story is more like thrilling, which they paired perfectly with the rest of the game. If you want a game where you look at the credits and think about the characters decisions, you are at the wrong store page. 6/10
Cons
-Takes a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of processing power. Do note that this is nothing the developers made a bad job with. It means that if you don't have a good pc enough, playing this game will become very difficult.
-Overall bad planning with the weapons. The fact that your weapon will do up to 60% less damage (I'm guessing) when overused. It gets passively annoying when you have to look for metal parts instead of bashing some zombies. This feature is being brought from Dead Island which even there made me grouchy.

Another thing you realise in this game is that you are bound to "the tower". This is your base, your safezone and your home. Leaving it is something that is risky, but necessary. Dying light is a very good game and I would highly recommend picking it up at some point.
-----Pros-----
Graphics - The game generally looked very good even on low settings, textures, lighting, models etc etc were well above what I was expecting
Optimization - playing on a laptop with 2.4ghz i7 and gtx 860m, the game was fine with almost no hick ups while on low and medium settings, and as i said before the game looked great while doing so
World Design - The levels in the game are designed for parkour, there is a lot of verticallity and complexity to the buildings and layouts. The world feels really good to explore in.
Movement - The parkour system is well done and easy to use. It feels rewarding to jump off zombies heads and slide under gates. works well both with keyboard and mouse and a controller.
Combat - the combat system is pretty expansive for a first person game featuring many different types of attacks. jumping attacks, grappling, ground slams, spinning moves. my only beef with the combat is that you can't block without a shield while human NPCs can. You are provided with a grapple and many other evasive manuevers in it's place though.
Interface - The games menues and HUD are well designed, information is provided at a glance.
Multiplayer - This is where the game really shines. Dying light is definitely one of the best current gen multiplayer games, almost full campaign coop besides the intro and the very last end mission. connecting to a game is easy, and in game connections are stable. the game also offers asymmetric pvp which looks really good but i haven't had the chance to try it yet. Only beef with the coop is your partner needs to be practically standing on your head before you can initiate dialogue with anyone.
DLC - The base game is good, and they are continuing to release solid content for it.
-----Cons-----
Difficulty curve- The game starts out very difficult, zombies take forever to kill and it really forces you to play stealthily and avoid confrontation to get things done. Once you start leveling things begin to change, weapon dmg goes through the roof and you are given many executes to finish off zombies in one or two hits.
NG+ and hard mode - I was dissapointed when i loaded into new game plus and switched the difficulty to hard mode hoping the game would take a massive difficulty boost. Zombies hurt more but they were still very easy to kill and avoid. It lacked that panicky feeling that was so prevelent in the first few hours of the game.
Weapon degredation - weapon degredation is crazy in this game, even more so than fallout and dead island. The part that really gets to me is the fact that you can't repair a weapon forever, it eventually needs to get referbished. I found only a single referbishing quest on my first play through.
Story - bland, love interest is really forced and awkward. connections to other characters seem superficial. The bad guy is cartoonishly evil and hard to relate to. Not so bad that the story takes away from the amazing gameplay.
Side missions - I have mixed feelings about the side missions although they were somewhat bland fetch quests you do meet the most interesting characters in these missions and your interactions with them develops a solid feeling for the world. After playing through The Oath in Felghana and Origin (once, for now), I finally got Ys I & II Chronicles+, expecting to get pretty much more of the same.
Man, was I in for a surprise.
The combat is EXTREMELY different. Instead of pressing buttons to use your weapon, you run into enemies to hurt them.
Yes, you run into them.
This is the first game I've ever seen to use such combat mechanics. And no, I'm not saying it's bad, but it really needs some getting used to, especially at the start of the game, when you have very low health and many monsters can kill you pretty quickly.
You also run into NPCs to talk to them, which can be annoying once in a while, because they tend to walk around aimlessly, often crossing your path, which leads you to run into them, which triggers a conversation (or a monologue, to be exact).
After you familiarized yourself with the combat, you shouldn't have too many problems along the way, although some of the boss fights might be a tad annoying (especially the end boss).
Other than the combat, the game is pretty much your standard fantasy action RPG. You have lots of characters to talk to, many places to visit, monsters to fight, equipment to get and so on and you really should pay close attention to everything or you might miss some rather important things. And I'm not talking story here, I'm talking equipment, that is rather vital to your survival and progress.
The game features not only a great soundtrack, but it also looks really nice. Reminds me of the good old action RPGs of the past, which this game actually is, too, as it was first released around 1988.
The combat is rather strange, but apart from that this is an absolutely great and fun game, albeit a bit challenging from time to time.
If you've played The Oath in Felghana and/or Origin, give this game a try, too, even though the combat is vastly different.
And if this is your first Ys game and you didn't like it (because of the combat), give Origin and The Oath in Felghana a try, because it has pretty much your standard action RPG combat.
Just finished Ys II, but as you can't write a separate review for it, I'll add it to the review on Ys I.
The sequel takes place pretty much right after the end of Ys I.
After killing Dark Fakt, you're transported to Ys, where you have to once again defeat evil.
The story is, obviously, pretty standard for a JRPG: save the world from evil and stuff.
Gameplay-wise it didn't change much, but additionally to the bump combat you now get to use magic, too, which I only used in the boss fights (where you have to use it, because most bosses are immune to melee attacks). The bump combat stayed pretty much the same, although I found it to be much easier to kill enemies now. Just run diagonally into them and keep on doing that and the enemy can't evade or counter in any way. You obviously have to look out for other enemies while doing that.
The graphics, imo, have aged pretty well. While it certainly isn't some fancy 3D stuff, the graphics look absolutely beautiful, especially when you consider that the game is over 25 years old.
The soundtrack, again, is quite good, too and you can even find the whole soundtrack in your Steam folder! And not just the new arrangements, but the original versions, too :)
If you liked the first game, then playing this should be a no-brainer, especially because you already own it anyway :P

Demon Peak advertises itself as a 2D platformer/metroidvania, and it's pretty okay at both.  Not amazing, but not terrible either. I didn't really know what to expect, but I didn't really have high expectations going in.  The platforming aspect itself feels great, the controls are tight and the movement is smooth, precise, and predictable. Same goes for the combat.  Janky controls/movement can completely ruin a game for me but I managed to finish this game in one sitting.
If you're looking for a story, you won't find it here.  Demon Peak gets straight to the point, which can be good or bad depending on what you're looking for.  The level design is pretty basic, the music is just OK (a little too intense and reptitive at times imo, can kinda get annoying), and sadly there are only a handful of enemies in the game, with even fewer boss fights.  Different "worlds" don't have different enemies, it's just the same uh.. demons.. throughout the entire game, which gets more than a little repetitive towards the end.  The handful of boss fights are pretty good though, aside from one which seemed like an afterthought.
The game world itself is pretty small, but I think that if it were a lot larger, the lack of variety with enemies would have just made the game seem tedious.  It's easy to get around, there are a save points similar to Super Metroid, and some secrets here and there.
The combat and movement is where this game actually shines.  It's fast, predictable, and precise in a way that you won't be blaming the game if you die--you'll know it's your fault.  Throughtout the game you acquire and buy different types of attacks, which are then used with button combinations similar to a fighting game, which are fun to use and most have their uses.  For $10 or whatever I paid (honestly I forgot tbh), I think it was a pretty good deal.
tl;dr:
Good:
-runs good
-gorgeous pixel art/animation
-great combat
-great movement
-pretty good boss fights
-decent amount of exploration
Bad:
-small/repetitive game world
-map needs work
-very small amount of enemies, gets reptitive near the end
-enemies don't change in different areas
It'll scratch the itch if it really needs scratching.

Nosferatu is a great game with some amazing ideas and bad programming.
Enemies have certain weaknesses and resistances against each of your weapons, encouraging you to use all of them, as each of them could be useful at any time.
Except the cane sword which is pretty much only used if you're out of ammo or just have a deathwish.
The layout of the castle is also pretty interesting, and has some fairly memorable rooms, with music that properly emphasizes the "Horror" aspect of the game.
Stinger sound effects play sometimes when you enter a room with nothing in it, it's completely silent as a ghoul sneaks up behind you. Overall a very unsettling experience, although most of it could be attributed to the aforementioned bad programming.
Characters will also die if you take too long exploring, creating a sense of urgency that may be offputting to some, or attractive to others. Although it does play into the story a bit, ie: the "sacrificing someone by a certain time of the day" trope.
However, this game is not very well made.
I've spent several agonizing minutes trapped in the furniture, or stray planks of wood, occasionally an opening door might push you into the wall, or into furniture.
Any time you jump, your character jolts suddenly upon hitting the ground at any speed or height. It's extremely annoying, especially when you combine those two things in the thankfully infrequent platforming. Admittedly, there really isn't any platforming at all, but there is the rare occasion when you might try to cross a gap, or climb to a higher level by stepping on some thin planks. You'll see what I mean, especially if you find a way to get the revolver early, or try to climb out of the trapdoor in a certain vampire's room.
There is also the fact that most of the time when you climb onto a roof or onto a gently ascending/descending elevator, your character shakes uncontrollably, making any movement extremely stuttered. The way you slide down rooftops could be intentional, but I sort of doubt it.
The hitbox for enemies is for the most part fairly consistent, but it's incredibly difficult to determine exactly what the effective range is on most of your weapons.
With all of this in mind, I still consider Nosferatu to be a very fun and unique game, sort of a Return to Castle Wolfenstein mixed with a bit of Castlevania.

Super Hexagon is a very simple survival action game. You are a triangle rotating around a hexagon to try to avoid getting crushed. Despite being simple in concept and in execution, this game is VERY HARD. Actually, that's an understatement. This game is ULTRA SUPER HARD. Ok, that may be an understatement as well. There are six levels of increasing difficulty. No matter the stage, the visuals are always your main enemy. The game has flashing colors, sorry for those who have epilepsy, and the stages rotate quite a bit. And by quite a bit, I mean ALL THE FREAKING TIME! The obstacles can be very tough to dodge on their own, but the rotations make what would be a very difficult game an uber-impossible challenge. Here's the overview of the stages you need to survive the full minute in literal terms on.
Hexagon: The easiest of the six, but still tough. The rotations aren't too annoying, but this stage does have something unique to it and a later stage: shape-shifting. At random, the hexagon will turn into a pentagon, and said pentagon can turn back into a hexagon or change into a square. This adds to the challenge as you *try* to adapt to the different geometry. The colors aren't too much of an issue.
Hexagoner: Instead of using shape-shifting this time around, we have the game trying harder to make your head hurt. The color scheme is more distracting, the rotations are more violent, and the obstacles come at you in a more complicated manner. Have fun with that.
Hexagonest: To this point, the game may be very tough, but beatable nonetheless. Well, if you just barely scraped by the two previous difficulties, I'm sorry to say that your journey is going to end here. This level contains even more annoying rotations and obstacles and an even more annoying color scheme. This will definitely cause you to rage if you aren't the patient type.
Hyper Hexagon: For beating each of the three previous stages, you unlock a hyper mode that REALLY ramps up the difficulty. In Hyper Hexagon, you WILL be thrown out the window in symbolic terms. Everything about the first level is buffed to insane levels of OMGWTF, with a WIDE range of colors, extremely fast rotations and quick and complex obstacles. All I can say is, if you beat the previous difficulties, you still aren't ready for what's to come.
Hyper Hexagoner: For beating Hexagoner, you get this lovely game mode, note my sarcasm. This mode uses a white background with the colors of the rainbow, so your head is REALLY going to be sent for a spin. Coupled with faster rotations and tougher obstacles, and you get a triple whammy that will beat you to a pulp before you even think about trying the last hyper mode.
Hyper Hexagonest: Otherwise known as Hell. Enjoy your stay, because it will be a VERY LONG STAY! With a grey color scheme that blends the overly difficult obstacles into the background, and the most violent rotations in any video game, your head may just turn into mush before you even make it halfway to the finish.
If you finish these six stages of pain and torture via LSD trip, you deserve to be put into the Video Game Hall of Fame. Unless you are prone to seizures, I definitely recommend Super Hexagon. Let's just say, this game is tough, but the fun type of tough, and it has some awesome songs to bout. All of this just for three dollars. Nice bang for your buck.

Divinity: Original Sin is an incredibly fun hardcore RPG. It is nothing like Diablo or Torchlight; if anything, it's more like Wasteland 2 (or 1) or the original Fallout 1 (or 2). It's best played with a friend. Please note that to create a co-op game, one player has to make a game with both players' characters. You don't just create a character and join your friend. You join your friend's game and take control of one of the characters (2-4, there are 2 main characters they create and you can recruit up to 2 other characters in the game, but personally I think the Lone Wolf perk is much better than another character). The game is absolutely MASSIVE. The first area in the game is a pretty big place with a surrounding area, and there's a place with LOTS of portals you activate later.
Here are some tips to new players:
- Steal every painting or gold ______ (such as Light Gold Cup) in the game! You can sell them for a lot, although this does make the money system rather unbalanced.
- Make sure to have characters that can do more than one thing! For example, a rogue-type character is great but knives mainly do piercing damage, which does very little to undead monsters, and there are a lot of those!
- Mages (Wizards, particularly) can be so useful, I'd almost call them overpowered. If you're going to be a mage, be sure to put points into every magic type (Aerothurge, Pyromancy, etc.); the more the better!
- When you're making a character, absolutely look at every aspect of it! If you don't like the perks or the spells you start with, change them!
- Last but not least, there are some Smelly Panties at the top of Esmeralda's house. They give Charisma +1.

There very little variety in the action, after a few hours you'll have encountered most of the scenarios you're ever going to. It VERY quickly gets really boring. I wish I loved this game.
I love the art, I love the music, I love tactical RPG's.
But I can not figure out the story; the choice options are not useful as either they are not what you want to do, are redundant such as: "say Ludin is no one; tell ludin to shut up and leave; or beat ludin up until he is quiet", and the choices don't always do what you want them to do.
I could get over this and see it as a more fun version of the Oregon Trail but there are 3 things that really bug me about this game.
Save Files, turn's and health/armor
You don't get any manual save options, instead the game generates auto save at some point (I can not tell when) and you have the classic "continue from your last thing" at one point my 'last play' and the last auto generated save where 10 days of travel and 7 battles apart not to mention key characters that died or did not die.
And the turn order in combat. I don't mind the I get 1 move then the opponent gets 1 move. But this system is seriously flawed when either you or the AI are outnumbered by the other, allowing your 3 units to move 2 times for ever 1 time their 6 units more.
It would be alot better if it had some turn order based on speed like Final Fantasy Tactics Advanced does, or if it was a simple 1 character move per 1 round like a lot of table top miniature games are.
You don't seem to be able to heal your health in battle and this is only annoying because you might have 3 health points left but still have 20 armor points. But because you can choose to attack health or armor, health weakens their life and their attack and attacking armor sometimes lets your next attack on that unit do more damage, there is no point in attacking armor. Enemies almost never attack armor and can hit you unit with a max health of 15 for 7 damage and then because you have 5 unit’s to their 2 that same enemy can get an extra turn to get your unit to 1 health and attack before he gets a move thus making him a wasted turn when he does come around.
In my eyes the whole point of an armor stat is either that it decreased the amount of damage you take, or they have to get through your armor to get to your health. However there is no point in enemies attacking your armor because they already do such massive damage while you have to hit their armor down to half if you want to do more than 3 damage to their health/strength stat a hit.

​I played this game entirely co-op with two friends, and we had a blast. The parkour is well done and quite fluid, and that fluidity of movement also factors into the melee combat. Gun combat isn't quite as polished, but it gets the job done. The crafting system allows you to make some pretty awesome melee weapons and can be quite satisfying.
All that being said, this isn't really a great game. I would not have finished it if I had been playing alone. The story is a boring, jumbled mess, and honestly we stopped paying attention to it half-way through the game. To make matters worse, the devs seem to take the story very seriously, and NPCs will talk on and on about the most mundane things. Luckily you can usually skip these conversations, though all of your co-op partners have to agree to skip (which wasn't a problem, we were all bored). And although the parkour works really well, the occasional platforming doesn't always work as well. Climbing towers, in particular, could be very frustrating.
I should also point out that, although this game is very co-op friendly, the very beginning and very end are single-player only. We found this very jarring, especially at the end when we had been playing together for dozens of hours and all of a sudden we were told we could only complete the game in single player. But for all my criticisms, the core gameplay loop, satisfying crafting, and solid co-op features make this an easy game to recommend if you have a couple of friends to play with.

As of the writing of this review the game has a mixed rating on steam.  Do not let that rating deter you from giving this game a shot, from my understanding when this game was released there were several bugs, such as maps that didnt work, save points which randomnly teleported you around the map, unfinished textures and other graphical bugs.  If I played the game in that state I probably would have given this game a negative review also, but all of these features have been fixed in the latest version.
The game itself is a standard metroidvania, but a very well done metroidvania.  Like most games of this type you have a decently sized map to explore and as you traverse the map you acqurie new abilities that help you access new areas.  You have some standard stuff like a double jump and the ability to breathe underwater, and a few unique items like spears which are a ranged weapon but can also be stuck to walls to be used as platforms.
Exploring the world is fun, you are always finding new upgrades and new combat moves which keeps things fresh, your character moves fast, the animation is fluid, and the controls are perfect.  Your character and his weapons look awesome and the world is varied with a wide variety of enemy types to fight.  You also get a some moves that are used with street fighter style inputs which I had a lot of fun with.   There are a total of 4 bosses, all of which are fun to fight and present a nice challenge.

Nyctophobia is a Horror adventure game, where the player’s objective is to escape the said location. The plot is bland for a ‘Lost in the Woods’ story, and a lot of the threats and pop-ups are either old-schooled or … questionable. Finding a skeleton hanging on a noose over a river doesn’t make any sense, unless the game has given some explanation behind the player’s finding.
As a horror game, I didn’t find anything intimidating apart from the tense music that would trigger at some points of the game. But even then, they were played at the wrong times, where no pop-ups or caution are present. In fact, the main figure that we need to avoid for the most part is the ‘Keeper’, who is nothing more than a mere silhouette. Honestly, I do not find a 2D cut-out exactly scary: especially at the last sequence, when I was being chased by it and had to reach reach the generator.
The overall design is pretty ick, and dispositioned to the point where I had to frown at certain physics and logic in the game. You’ll find the objects in game as unorthodox as a floating pack of Duracell batteries – Yes, this is exactly how you see the batteries, instead of them lying around like normal items. There isn’t many items or places that you can interact with either. When done, the effects, as the result of an action, are minimal and poor. For instance, when I used an axe to break down a wooden door, one would expect that it would have splintered and/or the door would fall in pieces. But nope – instead, the door fell flat like a domino, even glitching a bit before it fully collapsed.
The game simply did not fulfill it's part well as a Horror game. I wouldn't be motiavted to play thoroughly to the end, if it weren’t for the achievements. I would not recommend this game.

Not a playable game if you have motion sickness. The character moves so fast, is expected to change platforms so often, and the camera has no smoothing and directly moves with the character; it's very sickening. There are also various enemy attacks and the players own heavy attack which shake the screen; and there is no toggle option to turn it off.
Beyond this, although the graphics and animations are very nice; the combat itself is very spam based and badly structured. Player attacks do not stun or disrupt enemies and most of them have a decent amount of health and a moderate attack speed. Thus combat basically becomes a damage race of spam, the only way to really avoid it is by rapidly mashing the dodge button while trying to keep hitting the enemy. Which not only is awkward and inelegant, but is also impossible on smaller platforms. They could have made is so enemies have low health and thus die quickly, or made it so the players attack stun enemies; they did neither and the combat feels very unrefined because of it.
The environments aren't very impressive either, they really just are not shaped or designed in a way that makes them feel remotely immersive, real or in theme to the world. It just looks like the developers made a couple primitve ground and wall textures and then pasted them onto various pieces of geometry with a paltry amount of actual objects and decoration thrown in.
The fact that the game was essentially broken at launch and the developers barely patched it before abandoning it and trying to phrase it in a way that didn't make them sound like scum, also doesn't help.
Game may be worth the price for players really into this genre but as a general concept the game is not of a good quality.

If you got a low to mid range rig, CPUcores will help with performance.
It works, you'll be able to squeeze out extra fps or ensure a smoother, fluid gaming experience, reduced microstuttering etc however it varies from game to game and of course highly depends on your pc components. I'm seeing a 5-20 fps improvement across the board for various games. My specs are i7-3770K stock, 16GB ram, Sapphire Nitro+ RX580 and Plextor SSD, 1080p(basically a 5 yrs old rig), so you can roughly gauge how well CPUcores will help on your PC.
What it does NOT do is create a Miracle. Don't expect to run Witcher 3 on Ultra settings 1440p at constant 60fps on a $500 rig from 3 generations ago.
What it also does NOT do is boost performance on high end rig. If you already have a beast of a PC, this will not help a lot or at all. Why? Cos common sense, your rig is already overkill.

After 15 hours: If you like classic, turn-based RPGs (Fallout, Torment), take a look at this.
The combat is a new and cool approach to turnbased combat, and works really well. And the difficulty level is just perfect! You will continually get that epic win feeling, when you engage in combat with greater enemies.
The quests feel like they have meaning and are interesting, instead of the typical "kill these guys" or "get these things". There is not even a quest log, but just a journal that summarizes what you "already know". Basically just a reminder. You know... like a real journal? So you have to figure out YOURSELF, what the "quest" really is. It's heavily based on dialogue, and sometimes you have to really understand the purpose of the game's characters to know who to talk to about a certain quest. 'Cause the game wont tell you! Some dialogues even put you in really difficult moral decisions. Who gets to live, the young loner or the old family man? Should these soldiers be allowed to say they killed the monsters, even though you did, you they can get home to their families? More than once, I've stepped away from the computer to ponder my decisions.
Oh yeah, and it's got co-op, which I haven't tried yet. But so far, I have a feeling it would work really well. The dialogues are sometimes between your companions and you have actual discussions that have big effects on the outcome of a quest.
I've only played this for 15 hours total, so let's see if it can keep it up.

This is great for all those hardcore players who want to challenge themselves...
This is a rogue like game packed with action, enemies and abilities. You find coins in canisters or by killing enemies and can spend them on new items. These items each have a unique ability that improves your overall stats. Some of the ability's include flight, double jump, faster attacks, electric attacks and the list goes on and on.
You are cast onto an extra terrestrial planet and must do anything to survive the harsh 2d world. This game does not progress like most other games; when you die, you die, and you must restart right back from the start.
This game does however gradually get easier or harder, your choice. As you do certain things whithin the game you unlock newer characters that you can use whenever you want, each one with its own unique abilies. My favourite character would have to be the huntress, she can shoot while running, do several kinds of attacks with her bow and she can even teleport. As well as unlocking new characters you can also find artefacts in each level. Some artefacts can boost damage but lower defence, make enemies more tougher by turning them into their elite counterparts, make only one kind of enemy spawn in each level and many other artefacts that make the game either easier or even, harder.
I do however recomend that you use a controller to play (im using a steam controller) as the keyboard controls can be a pain sometimes.
Overall this is a pretty great game and I'd have to give it an 8 and a half out of 10.

The film contains three stories about three different dota players and their struggle towards winning TI. I think it's worth looking into and it's a pretty nice film which introduces Dota2. I sincerely hope this film could brought in more players and works as a window that helps people know more about this game and the whole industry.
However, I oppose this film firmly on their ways of depicting Chinese teams. This film deliberately pictured Chinese teams as the devil who dominates Dota2 arrogantly. It makes people feel that electronic gaming is more supported in China and people are open about electronic competitions so that's why they tend to win.
I admit that there's more players, so there's relatively more people who care about gaming but western countries have no idea what people think of games and how hard it is to be a professional player in China. A decade ago when warcraft and starcraft was popular in China, a journalist who played these games for about a couple hours wrote an article in the most popular newspaper in China stating that gaming is the "electronic heroine" which poisons youth and sabotages our nations' future. That article triggered a  national prejudice against gaming which crashed gaming industry in China. Ever since then gaming has became a "sin" which were never acknowleged as a normal career. Countless players fights for what they love despite family's objection. The environment was dire indeed, countless sponsors run away as soon as players won for they are greedy for the prize let alone teams who lost the tournaments. They couldn't even buy the tickets back home back then. The communities' passion on gaming builds up on the blood and sweat of those players who never showed up on big stages. There's no schools in China training players or set up careers for youth who love electronic competitions up till recently(9/17/2016).Lots of players giving up since high school and go training with other teams. They are mostly self- taught. All the champions and players fought so much for their success, their devotion to this sport and their thirst for winning is undeniable the best, and that's why they won.
Clearly this film omitted what I mentioned above to meet the expectation of the audience. Since they know so little about China and so few chinese watch this film, there's no point justify the winnings of the Chinese teams. I also think the interviews of the Chinese players are made up. They were told what to say which successfully fufilled the need of the film makers to lead people dislike Chinese players. This is what I can never tolerate, you can be ignorant and show nothing about Chinese players but that is clearly propagada.
Therefore, I want to express my disatisfaction about this film. Chinese are so competitive in this game and yet you know so little about Chinese players, their life and their career in real life. This film showed so little about Chinese teams. This showed a lack of responsibility of the Valve team.
I hope next time they may show the real life of the Chinese teams. In countries like China that people are just getting enough food a decade ago, it is a real feat following your heart and fight for what you love, it's no easier than the western teams.

It is with heavy heart that I cannot recommend this game.
I do like Risk of Rain, as should be obvious by how much I've played it. It does have some curious balance decisions that are a bit frustrating, but ultimately forgivable.
What's not forgivable are the bugs. I am on Linux and about one in every four games I play ends in a crash. I have scoured the internet, tried dozens of fixes, and I still get errors about missing Game Objects. This happens across two different computers running Ubuntu, and even on my windows machine the game has crashed on me a few times. The final straw is the fact that I cannot even unlock the miner because the game crashes every time the boss to unlock him spawns.
A few small things that would at least help mitigate the worst of the trouble would be making cloud saving a thing, and also making it so when you unlock something the unlock is instantly recorded into your save file, not at the end of the run. I don't know if this would be enough to make me want to play again but it would be a major step in the right direction.
It's too bad because without the bugs this would be an easy recommend, the art is great, the soundtrack is good, gameplay is overall dynamic and interesting, but with this many game breaking bugs I can't even enjoy it anymore.

I was engrossed from beggining to end. The Banner Saga delivers an engaging story, amazing bee-you-tee-ful art, and turn-based combat goodness amid an original and interesting setting/lore.
As the game starts, an ancient race of stone men that have mostly kept to themselves for centuries, are coming from the north en masse, killing, maiming and destroying. Thus, you are forced to leave your viking hunter-gatherer days behind and start a haphazard perigrination carrying your banner and leading your caravan. As you move on, you will be forced to make difficult decisions, manage supplies/people/morale and battle when necessary (or unavoidable).
Along the way, events will arise and you'll be faced with tough decisions. This is not Mass Effect 3 where you just choose in which way you kick♥♥♥♥♥even though the galaxy is supposedly being extinguished... here the severity of the situation means you'll be time and again counting your loses and licking your wounds.
It has minor drawbacks. Don't expect mindless AAA spectacle, I'm sure some people may find dialogue parts or other elements a bit sparse. You'll also jump between playable characters a couple times in an awkward, non-organic way. There was one instance where I was really getting into the story only for the game to yank me away to the other side of the map into some other character I had barely noticed before.
All in all, a great game that leaves me expectant for the sequels.

Half-Life 2 offers everything that is awesome about the original Half-Life game only going several steps further. The game takes place sometime after Gordon Freeman accepted a deal from the mysterious G-Man, Gordon had encountered throughout the Black Mesa lab facility during the Xem alien invasion. The G-Man appeared to know more about the situation at Black Mesa than he's leading on to. After that ill fated day Gordon awakens from a status sleep mode and is once again greeted by the G-Man who gives Gordon a trippy light show straight out of the Twilight Zone opening. After the G-Man giving out his monologe, Gordon soon finds himself on a train accompanied by people all wearing the same clothing. The train docks at what appears to be a city but not like any city Gordon has ever visited or seen before. He knows it is Earth and not the Xem planet, because most of the posters and signs are in European text. The city itself is called "City 17" an enclosed society with marshall law as a form of enforcement as there are various security cameras, hover cameras, weaponized mechas, armored swat like policemen, force fields, & tanks. As Gordon wonders through the train station and soon the city itself, he feels alienated as he apparently has been gone from Earth much longer than expected. While trying to make sense of things, he soon finds himself being chased by the police during a raid taking place in an appartment building. When all seem lost for Gordon, he is saved by a woman name Alyx who is the daughter of Dr. Eli Vance whom Gordon knew from Black Mesa. Alyx leads Gordon to a hidden base being opperated by a group of freedom fighters who all want to be freed by the Combine, the organization that is controlled by the Xem that enslaved the entire planet after the Black Mesa incident occured. Gordon immediately makes a few new friends and even meets some of the last surviving Black Mesa staff members who are all more than happy to see Gordon alive and well. After the introductions and reunion Gordon learns about the situation of the city and how to help the freedom fighters win their freedom. The main goal is to destroy the Combine's main base of operations in the center of the city which leads Gordon into a long journey ahead. But with the use of his EMV suit that he reacquires and the assortment of weapons nothing will stand in his or his friend's way towards freedom. Half-Life 2 has so much to offer that I don't know where to start. Well first of all the graphics are improved up a notch and the glitches that were in the first game are no where in site. The enviroments are huge and vast, I could just spend hours sinking in all that is offered in site. The new characters are as great as well as the returning ones, Alyx is a great addition to the franchise someone in which the female fan base can immediately associate with. The method of killing enemies are the same as in the original as with the vast assortment of weapons you have multiple ways to kill certain enemies. The plot contains elements straight outta the novel 1984, the films the Matrix, THX-1138, Alien, The Thing, & The Fly. Every minute of this game I enjoyed to the fulliest, if you liked the original Half-Life then you'll love this game even more. It's proof that a game's sequel can be better than the original and this one takes that title. Half-Life 2 is what legends are made of. I might be ranting on about it for too long, but I am dead serious. The game is more than a high recommendation, it is mandatory you play this game. You have not lived life to its fullest until you have played this game.

Alrighty. Nosferatu: Wrath of Malachi.
This one has been on my radar for a good while. I recently started playing Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth and discovered Clive Barker's Undying, so i've been on a late 90's-early 2000's survival horror kick of late.
PREMISE:
Rescue your family members from a sprawling castle before they are sacrificed and deal with that vampire infestation using victorian-era weaponry and holy artifacts.
PLOT:
Nothing really special about the game's plot, as it follows a man whose poor but noble family has traveled to a spooky castle (red flag 1) for the marriage of their daughter to a mysterious suitor of great wealth and influence (Red flag 2). He gets there and everybody's missing (red flag 3) and the main door has a TON of crucifixes bolted to it (red flag 4).
He has to rescue his family members and destroy Malachi's servants. The plot is very minimalist, but it works pretty well for the feel of the game as it's a lot like playing through an early horror film.
GAMEPLAY:
Quite a bit like Clive Barker's Undying. Strafe and bunny hop through Castle Malachi like it's the 90's. There are a decent variety of enemy types that you'll be fighting with a machine gun (acquired quite late in the game), a musket, a revolver, a flintlock pistol, stakes, a holy chalice, a crucifix, your trusty cane sword and your bare fists.
The weapons all feel pretty good, but the standouts here are the crucifix and the chalice. Channel your inner Van Helsing by making regular water holy using your crucifix and the throwing it from the chalice for massive damage. The stakes are also interesting because of the ability to use them as torches and to impale vampiric foes before they rise from their coffins.
The servants of Malachi include all manner of things that go bump in the night and each contributes to the challenge in its own way. For example, some enemies will scared of the crucifix, while others can be killed outright by it and some are immune. This helps to keep things interesting as you Keanu Reeves your way through this spookshow. The boss fights are made up of the more powerful vampiric servants of Lord Malachi, with a few surprises. Stock up on that holy water whenever you can.
The really interesting thing about the gameplay here is that it progresses in real time. Near the beginning, you'll be informed that one character has only thirty minutes to live. Watching the clock, you have to find him a doctor. Each character in the castle can die, both at a scheduled sacrifice time and as you are escorting them to the safe area. After they make it to safety, they open their trunk to give you useful weapons and items. However, the actual act of escorting your surviving family members is where I have a problem. While it's not gamebreaking, the AI of your followers is very, very dated. Sometimes they struggle with doors, block you, or stop following you without any notice so you have to backtrack to find them standing with their face in a wall somewhere. It should be noted that enemy AI is of decent quality, and the game can be quite difficult early on as a result.
GRAPHICS:
Nothing really special here either save for some pretty cool cutscenes and a vintage film line / grain effect that does a lot to sell you on the idea that you're in a silent movie from the early 1900's. I personally rather enjoy the look of the game, however. The environments are good, and the atmosphere is suitably spooky. The dark corridors and tombs of Castle Malachi definitely nail the look of old horror films, which is exactly what I was paying (and hoping)  for.
SOUND:
It goes with the time, but the SFX are fairly robotic and clunky. The monster sounds are hokey and fun, but the voice acting is quite stiff. As far as technical issues go, however, there's only really one. As is the case with most games released in 2003, you can definitely tell when a dialogue byte is playing due to a slight his and the occasional pop. These aren't likely to be noticeable; I am simply very picky about audio. These can be overlooked though, as the music in the game is good. Dramatic horror sweeps and suspense tones are used to a good effect and contribute to the gameplay by alerting you to nearby perils. Again, the atmosphere is pretty much nailed here.
FINAL OPINION:
Nosferatu: The Wrath of Malachi is a great choice for any fan of Bram Stoker's Dracula. It suffers from a few of the flaws that most games from the early 2000's had, but it makes up for them in atmosphere, fun combat, and creative ways to fight the undead. The game takes about 3-4 hours to complete, so it's rather short. It's also only $10 and it's one i'll almost certainly be playing through again on the hardest difficulty.
FINAL RATING:
8.5 / 10
